utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. If I could remained you, Mr. Theunens, of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence, which still applies.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning Your Honours, good morning everyone. Good morning, Mr. Theunens. I would like to ask you something. In view of the time limit, would you please, whenever possible, give me a yes or no answers, and if you think there is a need to explain something, then please do. Yesterday we spoke about documents that are kept in war units, and if I were to tell you that the operations diary or operations log that we mentioned yesterday is a document where a daily recording is made of all activities, reporting and everything that's going on in the unit, would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the question mentions war units. Now, what I get from the JNA regulations, and I refer to Exhibit 397, which is the JNA battalion manual from 1988, it's actually the war diary that contains such information. And an operations diary will contain information that is related -- if it is important that is related to non-war, or non-combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we -- or, rather, here we heard some other testimony, but that's fine, we will accept this as your opinion. When drafting your report, you asked that operations log and other documents of the units that you were analysing be provided to you, especially the log of the guards brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I want to come back to the first part of the question because it says we will accept it as your opinion. I can read out from the quotation of the battalion manual where it says that: "The war log-book or war diary is kept every day throughout the war. All events or other important information are entered into it chronologically." I will not read out from the rest of that paragraph, but it is, for your information, paragraph 114 of Exhibit 397. Now, we did request the operations log of the guards brigade from Serbia and Montenegro, but we haven't received it yet, and if you wish so, I can give you the references and the dates of that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, we're really using up a lot of time in our answers. Did I understand you well that you said that in the battalion manual it is prescribed how a war log-book is kept? Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the battalion manual it is mentioned that -- it is mentioned what a war log-book or what a war diary is, but there is no -- I haven't seen a template for how the war diary should be arranged. I think I have seen such a template in the brigade manual, the 1984 brigade manual, which is Exhibit 395.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, if I were to tell you that a war diary or war log-book was never kept at the level of a battalion, but rather at the level of larger units, such as corps and brigade -- or, rather, regiment and brigade, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, I have the similar entry in my report that war log-books are diaries. All diaries are kept at all units/command levels above the battalion level, and this is on page 60 of the English version of my report, part 1. But the quotation I made comes from the JNA battalion manual from 1984, paragraph 114, and this is known in this trial as Exhibit 394.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Now let us go back to the documents that you sought in order to write your expert report. These documents were not provided to you -- or, rather, you did not receive a number of documents that you believed to be relevant for your expert report, those pertaining to the Operations Group South.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we received a first batch of documents, I think at the end of 2002 or early 2003, which consist of 47 documents. Most of them were orders and reports by Operations Group South, as well as the 1st Military District. Those were very helpful documents. Among them was, for example, the resubordination order from OG South. If I'm not wrong, it's the order 446-1 from the 21st of November, 6.00 in the morning, which is the Exhibit 420 in this case. Now, it was obvious that some documents were lacking, and again I've prepared an overview of RFAs, request for assistance, where the replies are incomplete or non-existent, and only for the RFAs I drafted between December 2002 and May 2006 we come to a number of 40, where no replies were given, or the reply was given that the documents do not exist, even though in some cases they have been used by the Defence with military witnesses, or were mentioned by military witnesses during interviews. And in some cases we received only partial replies. Obviously there are, in addition to these 40 requests, there are other requests where we did receive a satisfactory reply to -- yeah, to our requests.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you explained that to us yesterday and you are repeating that again today, and I think that we, on account of that, will run into a problem with time. My next question: Do you believe that your expert report is actually incomplete, given that you did not receive these documents from the Ministry of Defence, especially the portion pertaining to the activities of the Operations Group South?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I believe that the documents I did have access to, documents from OG South and the 1st Military District, allow me or have allowed me to provide an accurate picture of the activities and in particular the command and control situation within OG South during the time period that is relevant for this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: On page 6 of your expert report, page 6 both in the B/C/S and English version, paragraph 10, you say that operations and tactical groups may be established during operations in order to facilitate command and control. My question is: Are these groups established in circumstances when establishment units are not fit to carry out certain tasks and assignments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, in part 2 of the report, section 2, on the pages 53 and until 55 for the English version, I give an overview for operational groups and tactical groups that were established in other parts of Croatia during the operations there. And my understanding, or my -- from these orders is that operational groups and tactical groups, and in the case of OG South, assault detachments and assault groups, were established to maintain single command and control, or single authority, I should say, as well as unified command and control. Because we see that these operational groups consist of JNA units, units of the Territorial Defence of Serbia, in a number of cases units which could be called local Serb TO units as well as volunteers and even paramilitaries, and because of the wide diversity in the origin of these units, some of them have never worked together prior to these combat operations, a requirement was felt by the commanders, and in most cases they're corps commanders or military district commanders, to establish operational groups and lower-level ad hoc units like tactical groups, assault detachments and assault groups. And I just want to add when I use the expression "paramilitaries," I mean it in the sense of forces which are -- when reviewing the legal framework could be considered illegal. So armed formations which are not under the strict control from their origin by the authorities which are allowed to operate and to carry weapons and to participate in military operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you have explained that in your expert report. Yesterday you gave a very brief, condensed answers to the questions put by my learned friend. I ask that you do the same in relation to my questions. We have very little time remaining. Tell me, please, if I were to tell you that an operations group is established by the military district command, and according to the rules it should have under it at least a unit at the level of the land forces corps, which means that it could be reinforced by one or more brigades. Would you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be -- that could be one of the possibilities, Your Honour. The examples I have quoted from indeed show that operational groups are established by military districts. And on page 54 I speak of Operational Group 3, which was established by the 5th Military District. Now, where the subordinate units are concerned that varies of the operational group. I cannot give a categorical answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If an operations group is established, would there be a special command for that operations group, would that be established as well, or would the corps command be reinforced by a number of staff officers who would then exercise command over that unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the examples I studied, and in particular OG South, show that in relation to Operations Group South there was already an Operations Group South prior to the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade, but quite soon and according to the war diary, which is -- the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade, it's the command, i.e., the staff and the other officers in the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade who take over the command of OG South, and the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade becomes the commander of OG South, replacing the previous commander, Bajo Bojat.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The previous Operations Group South, before the arrival of the guards brigade, and after it arrived in the first eight days, did it have a special command, a special command established by the military district command, headed by Bajo Bojat?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, indeed, like any other unit, Operational Group South had a command. I -- based on the information I had access to, I'm not able to establish who created that command of OG South and where these officers who operated or were part of the command of OG South prior to the arrival of the Guards Motorised Brigade in the Vukovar area originated from.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that based on the military rules it wasn't possible to establish an operational group at the level of the brigade, and especially that it wasn't possible for a brigade command to grow into the command of the Operations Group South command because it simply didn't have enough personnel and wasn't qualified enough to exercise command, what would you say to that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I can -- I can provide three elements of reply to that question, Your Honours. First of all, I think General Zivota Panic, who unfortunately died I think two years ago, was the commander of the 1st Military District and who, according to open-source material I reviewed, established Operational Group South, while it was his judgement as a commander to -- and his decision to establish Operations Group South and to have the Guards Motorised Brigade take over the command of Operational Group South. A second element is that based on my review of JNA documentation, the Guards Motorised Brigade was not just a motorised brigade. It was a very strong brigade. For example, it had two military police battalions, it had the best manpower, it had the most modern equipment. I quote from Narodna Armija article in my report, where mention is made of M-84 tanks in the armoured battalion of the Guards Motorised Brigade. Now, the third element or final element I would like to mention, from the documents I reviewed, which are also included in my report, we see that the command of the guards brigade and its staff was --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, what do tanks have to do with the command? Please focus on the question or else we will be wasting a lot of time. I asked you about the command of the operational group and the rules regulating how an operational group is established.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think Mr. Vasic would understand that the composition of a unit will be reflected in the command and vice versa. If you have a large high-quality unit, I mean high-quality by its personnel and by its equipment, then that will obviously also be reflected in the nature of the command of that unit on whatever level we're talking about, whether it's a brigade or a corps or another unit. So that's why I thought it was useful to mention that. The third element I wanted to provide was that additional officers were sent to the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade already prior to the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade taking over the role as commander of OG South, and I think of Colonel Pavkovic, and there was also I think Colonel Tesic, but I'm not hundred per cent sure of the last name. It's mentioned in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Please tell me, would you agree with me that what you write in your expert report and what you call an OG South in your report is actually a temporary formations which has all the features of a tactical unit, not an operational one.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wish to emphasise it's not me who came up with the name Operational Group South. I think from the documents that have already been exhibited in this case prior to my testimony it is, for example, visible that Colonel Mrksic signs the orders he issues as the commander of OG South. He still does that on the 23rd of November in the Exhibit 426, which is a report 500-1 to the 1st Military District. Now, it could be discussed whether it's an operational level unit or a tactical level unit or a tactical/operational, but based on my understanding of JNA doctrine or SFRY armed forces doctrine that applies to command and control, its functions and principles, that distinction it not relevant. So distinction whether it's tactical, operational or strategic is not relevant in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that when an Operations Group South, its commander only has temporary command of it, which was transferred to him by the commander establishing an operations group [as interpreted]?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. But as I said, that doesn't change anything to his -- his -- his duties or his role as a commander. Nor his command and control functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: So the order of the superior command establishing an operations group should give a certain scope of command competences and authorities to the commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That may be a possibility, Your Honours. Now, I wish to mention that on the 5th of August, 2005 we requested from Serbia and Montenegro all orders by the SSNO or the 1st Military District to appoint Colonel Mrksic as commander of the guards brigade, to appoint him to the position of command of Operational Group South, and obviously such an order would have included information on the powers of Colonel Mrksic. Now, we have received a reply on the 15th of November, 2005 whereby the competent authorities of Serbia and Montenegro informed us that they still need to reply to the RFA. On the 3rd of November, 2005, we received a similar reply, and on today we have not received such an order. Coming back now to the documentation that was available to me, and I mean by this orders signed or issued by Colonel Mrksic between 8th of October and the 23rd of November, as well as reports he sent to his superiors, I don't have the impression that there were any --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens --

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to his command powers during the time period he was commander of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I kindly ask that you focus on my questions. My question was what is contained in the order establishing an operations group. I didn't ask you anything further than that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't think it would be helpful to give a hypothetical answer on what should be or could be included in such an order. I tried to provide an answer that actually is related to the issues we are discussing here.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what were the objectives and tasks of the Operations Group South as a temporary combat formation, and could that only be learned from the order establishing it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, because we don't have the order for the establishment of Operations Group South, I cannot testify as to what is included in that order. Now, in my report in the second part on page 61, on the top of the page there is a description, the importance of Vukovar, which is based on an interview with General Zivota Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: The importance of Vukovar is just that; the importance of Vukovar. I asked you about objectives and tasks. But, all right. Tell me, please, based on the rules, is an operations group supposed to be disbanded after a task is accomplished?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I forgot to add one element, and I will be short. But obviously each order for operations of the operational group or subunits of the operational group will include taskings, and from that it will be obvious what the subordinate units have to do. To answer this question, yes, indeed, an operational group should be disbanded, but that's the prerogative of the commander who established the Operational Group South. And from the documentation I reviewed, I mentioned the exhibit from -- the document from the 23rd of November. The Operational Group South still existed on the 23rd of November, 1991. And it was Exhibit 426, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Did you see the order on disbanding of the OG South, and does it exist?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen it, Your Honours. But if the commander of Operational Group South on the 23rd of November still sign as report with -- under his name, his official assignment, i.e., the commander of Operational Group South, it is obvious that the Operational Group South still existed on the 23rd of November, 1991. Otherwise he would have signed as commander, Guards Motorised Brigade, in this case, or with another title.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In your expert report you said that large combat operations are very complex and require detailed planning and taking into account factors at every level of command, and that this becomes ever more complex at every level. Could it then be said that the decision of the commander of the 1st Military District to include the guards brigade into the Operations Group South without reinforcing it jeopardised the mission of that brigade and brought it into situation where it was not fit to effectively carry out the assignment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on public statements General Panic made, for example, his interview for the BBC series "Death of Yugoslavia" after the events, it appears -- or the message he is sending is actually that the guards brigade was sent because it was such a high-quality unit, whereas the other units that had been sent to the area were incapable of accomplishing the mission, which, according to Zivota Panic, consisted of, I quote, "Liberating Vukovar." Now, from the personal records of General Mrksic we discussed briefly yesterday, there was an entry on the -- on the way how he accomplished his duties as commander of OG South, and I think it was a very positive assessment he received there. I haven't come across any document where General Mrksic or somebody else in OG South or in the 1st Military District indicates that the Guards Motorised Brigade or -- I mean its units or the command or General Mrksic is incapable of accomplishing the mission. Or has difficulties to accomplish that mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: In your report you spoke about the TO. Will you agree with me that TO staffs are never resubordinated, only TO units are. Upon completing their mission, they're back under the command of TO staffs, as rule, aren't they? I'm just asking your opinion on that. Resubordinating TO staffs.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean the doctrine is discussed in part 1. In the second part I talk about resubordination of TO units. But I think it's very important to highlight, and I've tried to do that in the report, that the units which are described as TO and which were operating under the command of OG South, and I mean by this in particular Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica, are not the unit -- are not TO units as they were initially conceived in the doctrine of All People's Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I asked you about the resubordination of TO staffs. Is it possible to have a TO staff resubordinated at all? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give a yes or no answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What sort of an answer could you possibly provide then?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean I would -- I would direct your attention to the first part of the report, starting on page 92 where there is -- it's in the part number 5, where I discuss the organisation of the TO as it actually was prior to 1991, its structure. The command and control issues in relation to TO are discussed on --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: My apologies, my sincere apologies, Mr. Theunens. I simply asked you about TO staffs. I didn't ask you about command and control at the republican level or at the local level or at any level at all. My only question to you is: Can TO staffs be resubordinated? Do you know that, do you not know that? Yes, no, can you answer? Can you not answer? Let's try not to waste any more time, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, but I mean I -- I would like to help you or to assist you, but it would helpful for me if you would clarify whether we are talking about the TO or the units known as TO that were operating in Vukovar in October, November 1991, and even prior to that; or are we talking to the Territorial Defence as it existed in each of the republics and the autonomous provinces prior to the outbreak of the conflict in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: That's fine, Mr. Theunens. I think we should move on, because our time is slowly running out. On page 119 of the B/C/S of your report, and I believe the English page is 110, you quote an order by the commander of OG South ordering the establishment of command posts pursuant to an order of the 1st Military District. The exhibit number is 374. Were local commanders then ordered to follow the relevant rules for garrisons and barracks in carrying out this order?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. I just wish to make a correction to the -- to the transcript. It says on the line 10:04:43, "ordering the establishment of command posts." "Komanda mesta" in B/C/S in this context means -- I think should be translated as "town commands" into English, which is a significantly different thing from a command post. And the answer is yes to the question of Mr. Vasic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is not about town commands. I'm talking about local commands, local-level commands. In the B/C/S that is perfectly clear. That is what I'm asking you about. Sir, is not one of the duties of a local commander to ensure order and discipline at that particular command and in those particular units, as well as to inform the leaders or commanders of any units passing through the area under his command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, ensuring order and discipline at a command is a task for any commander. Ensuring order and discipline in units is actually one of the duties of an operational commander. I mean by operational commander a unit commander from the highest level to the lowest level. And inform the leaders or commanders of any units passing through the area under his command, I don't understand what you mean by this. Because how can the town commander inform them? I would see it in a different way, in the opposite way. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you are a military expert. I'm asking you about the duties concerning the rules relating to the garrisons and barracks. This is Article 83 of the rules. We're talking about an entire area of activity of a command whereby the command tries to maintain discipline, lay down the rules for -- for its area, and also tries to inform any units that happen to be passing through its area of these rules that obtain. How about that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I have answered the question. Now, if we talk about this Exhibit 374, it also mentions -- it talks about actually town commanders. Because in the fourth paragraph, Mrksic says, "I appoint as commanders for Vukovar town the commanders of the assault detachments for the part of the town within their operation zone." And I wish to add at the end it says: "Prevent any ill treatment of the population and local inhabitants and unauthorised entry and searches of apartments and houses." That goes much further than the duties of a garrison commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Under the rules for garrison and barracks, does a commander not also have the duty to ensure discipline and order also in all detention units in his area? Isn't this something that Article 3 of the rules on the armed -- 83 on the rules of the armed forces also envisages?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's difficult for me to answer the question because I don't have the rules of the armed forces or the document described here as the rules of the armed forces in front of me. Do you mean by this that the 1984 law on the service in the armed forces or another document? 1985, sorry, 1985 law on the service in the armed forces or another document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I mean the rules governing the work of the armed forces, regulating what goes on in the garrisons and barracks and the service in garrisons and barracks. That's what I had in mind. But we could as well move on. Would you agree with me that the commander of OG South, in his regular combat report, highly confidential 431, the date is the 19th of November, 1991, and the number is 419. In another confidential order, the number is 349-1, appointed commanders of Grabovo, and then on the 17th of November appointed another commander?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: On account of the extreme speed at which the names were read out, the interpreters did not catch the names. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: I said that pursuant to this order Slobodan Misovic was appointed local or town commander. When he left the area of responsibility on the 17th of November, 1991, the person appointed was Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Vojnovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I remember that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Vojnovic, as the commander of Jakubovac, Ovcara and Grabovo had the same responsibilities as all the other local commanders there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, he would have the same -- Vojnovic would have the same responsibilities as all the other town commanders or locality commanders, based on the order that Mrksic -- or that the person appointing him had issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic, in his order, highly confidential 32-1 of the 19th of November, introduced his authority as -- or, rather, transferred his authority as the local commander of Ovcara to a captain whose name we are now unable to mention, but you know who this person is because there is a reference to this person in your own report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I am familiar with this order by Colonel Vojnovic, and I am also familiar with the fact that the unit of that captain was -- had been subordinated to the Guards Motorised Brigade at a much earlier stage and it is actually referred in the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade. But I am unable to -- I mean, without seeing the war diary to mention -- to give you the exact date. I think it's on the 5th of October -- or the 5th of November, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: We may come back to this later on, if there is time. I will show you a report dated the 16th of November, based on which you can see that this unit is a member of the 80th Brigade at the time, but we will be back to that in due time. Can you agree with me that the commander of OG South in his order 439-1 dated the 20th of November, 1991, which is Exhibit number 419, again warned the local commanders in the zone of operations of OG South to take all measures necessary to ensure the proper functioning of military authorities in keeping with his previous order dated the 9th of November, 1991, underlining the need to prevent any harassment or mistreatment of civilians or anyone who happens to be in the area of that particular local command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Even without having the order in front of me, it's -- it is discussed on the English page 112. Now, as we mentioned yesterday, when discussing the functions of command and control, issuing an order or giving an assignment which is the same -- is one thing, verifying its implementation, i.e., control, is another thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: What about this order, the order that we've referred to, 419-1, dated the 20th of November? Did the commander of OG South not order an evacuation of the sick and wounded from the Vukovar Hospital with no reference to prisoners of war as a special category? The number is 439-1.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and it's Exhibit 419. And it says in the orders, so to the subordinate units: "Simultaneously evacuate and transport civilians, the wounded and the sick from the hospital in Vukovar." And this is discussed on page 97 and 98 of the second part of the report in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, this is Exhibit 419, and Exhibit 419 says -- can one conclude based on this that the commander of OG South ordered nothing in relation to the prisoners of war who were in the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is the question limited to this order or is it a general question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: It's in relation to the order that we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just read out that Colonel Mrksic ordered to simultaneously evacuate and transport civilians, wounded and sick from the hospital in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your report you mention the order, strictly confidential 464-1, signed on the 21st of November, 1991 by the Chief of Staff, Miodrag Panic - this is Exhibit 422 - invoking the order of the 1st Military District, 115-51, dated the 20th of November. Have you seen the substance -- or the substance of this order of the 1st Military District mentioned here is about?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the order 115-151 of the 1st Military District dated 20th of November?

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's among the orders we have requested earlier from Serbia and Montenegro but didn't obtain. But it was in one of the packages I think you prepared to cross-examine Prosecution witnesses, military witnesses, who appeared here before me. I have read it, but I don't recall what exactly is in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I tell you that this is an information report and not an order, would that jog your memory?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding is that 115-151 is an order, and it's described as such in Exhibit 422, i.e., the order 464-1 issued by Operational Group South on the 20th -- on the 21st, excuse me, at 6.00 in the morning and signed by Panic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you agree with me that the Chief of Staff, pursuant to instructions governing the work of commands and staffs signs the order himself in the absence of the commander and that he then assumes the role and position of the commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is correct that the Chief of Staff is also the Deputy Commander and can, for example, sign orders or order documents during the absence of the commander. But I haven't been able to determine whether the fact that a commander is absent removes his command responsibility. Based on the -- on the JNA doctrinal documents that were discussed yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm not talking about commander responsibility; I'm talking about the function. When the commander is not there, does the Chief of Staff not sign the orders, and does he, in fact, not in the commander's absence stand in for that commander?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. But I just wanted to clarify the -- whether the Deputy Commander or the Chief of Staff takes over all the duties of the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can we please have Exhibit 375 on our screens. This is the war log of the 80th Brigade. Can we please show the entry dated the 19th of November at 1800 hours. Mr. Theunens, in this part of the war log of the 80th Brigade -- could we please zoom in a little on the lower part of the page. This is the entry in relation to the 19th of November at 1800 hours. Can we please show the English, since the witness is expected to read what it says or agree with what I am about to read out to him. Mr. Theunens, it says here that in the morning hours the Ustashas who had been captured were taken to the Sremska Mitrovica prison. Combat is underway in the hospital sector, where the remaining ZNG and MUP members, about 200 of them, are expected to surrender. The war log, the 19th of November, 1800 hours. An order has been issued to be at the ready to organise the guarding of prisoners. Do you believe that -- 19th of November, 1800 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honours. I don't know if there is a technical problem. We're not receiving the document that they are referring to. I don't know if the rest of the court is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Nobody is yet receiving it. We are looking at the wrong date. We've now moved to the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The screen shows the 10th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've now got the right date coming up.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We need the 19th, 1800 hours. That's the entry we're after. That should be the one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps believe that an order like this could have come from the OG South command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, from this entry it's -- one can assume, one can make an assumption that orders have been -- that an order has been issued, but it is not necessarily the case. Because what I read here in English is that -- I will not read the first one, but then: "And so it was arranged to be prepared about the organising..." and then between slashes, "security of the prisoners." Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, just a second. We've discussed this before this Chamber already, and this is about an order. It's not about organising. I think that much is clear, for the simple reason that the B/C/S version happens to be the authoritative version of this particular text.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, Mr. Vasic, yesterday yourself you raised the issue about me being influenced by witness statements or other testimony, I try to look at now this document based only on the document I have in front of me and the other documents I have seen, I tried to be not influenced by what other witness may have said or testified or not. I cannot draw from this English translation which is in front of me --

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I fully understand you, but you are looking at the English. The English is a translation of the original B/C/S, and what it reads is: "An order has been issued." So this is not about evidence given by witnesses. The logic inherent to the staff system of command, would it not point to the conclusion that an order like this about future treatment of prisoners issued by the command would indicate that the command has taken a responsible attitude in terms of treating prisoners of war, a command that issues an order like this, if indeed that was the command of OG South?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it would have been helpful to have a correct English translation then. But in any event, if an order has been issued then such an order had to be -- because of the principle of single authority had -- should have been issued by the commander of OG South to its subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Vasic, you have now overrun just on 10 minutes. So we have to say that's the end.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have four questions left, Your Honours, that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... so many hours in the day, Mr. Vasic, and if you take extra time, it means that in the end Mr. Lukic misses out again. I just have to be even between people, you see. If there's one question you see as very important, have that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. It's something to do with the previous question, and I think that is very important indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that in keeping with this order dated the 19th of November, 1800 hours, the one that we have now mentioned from the log-book, Lieutenant-Colonel Vojnovic acted in the spirit of this, order. This you mention on page 100 of the English and 108 of the B/C/S when ordering that the shifts of guards be determined in order to guard the ZNG and MUP members who had been captured and also enlisted the assistance of the military police brigade and company of the 80th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on the entries that were read out now, it is not possible for me to determine on which basis the brigade commander, i.e., Vojnovic, requested rotation of officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: This is not rotation; these are guard shifts. But never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. VASIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have lots of questions left for this witness, but unfortunately, in view of the constraints, I will have to finish now. I hope that I can use the assistance of other witnesses to clarify some issues which I have not been successful in clarifying right now with this witness. Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vasic. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. I am Borivoje Borovic, attorney-at-law, Defence counsel for Miroslav Radic. Yesterday in your evidence you said, or rather you quoted, among other things, the book of General Kadijevic. You mentioned that he had written that the goals of the JNA in Croatia were defined in a certain way, namely, to protect and defend Serbs from Croats and to lift the siege of barracks, for example, the one in Vukovar, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, these -- the two objectives that Mr. Borovic just read out are two of -- are only two of the objectives Kadijevic listed in his book, and -- I mean, this is discussed on the pages 6 through 11 of my report. Unless you want me to go in detail, I would just limit myself to listing these pages, because Kadijevic also mentions other goals, including the liberation of the Serbian territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is: Based on what did you conclude in your report that the role of the army was reduced to reinforcing Serb or Serbian control in the portions of areas in Croatia? Would you be so kind and explain what you meant by that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I based myself on what Kadijevic writes in his book, together with contemporaneous, I mean by that statements from 1991, and documents from 1991 that were issued by Kadijevic and Adzic, which are discussed in that particular section of the report. If you wish, I can quote from what Kadijevic writes. He, for example, speaks about two phases in the conflict, and maybe we can just limit ourselves to the second --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can I ask you something, Mr. Theunens. I accept this, but I'm afraid that I will run out of time too. My question is: Where did you find, in which interviews and books, this claim, namely that the role of the army was reduced to reinforcing Serbian control in Croatian territory? Do you differentiate between "Serb" and "Serbian," these two terms in your report. First of all, would you tell us that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, do you ask me a grammatical question to explain what is the difference between "Serb" and "Serbian," or do you want me to mention to you the quotation -- a quotation from Kadijevic's book that actually supports this analysis?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In your report you use both terms. So, no, I'm not referring to a grammatical error. You say "Serb," and then in parentheses, you say "Serbian control." In order to clarify to the Trial Chamber, would you please explain what's the difference between "Serb control" and "Serbian control." I'm taking this out of your report. Paragraph 18, page 9 of the first part of your report.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reference is actually different, but I understand your question now, and I apologise for failing to do so initially. "Serb" means or refers to Serb outside of Serbia; and "Serbian" would refer to Serb within Serbia. And if I remember well, this is something I found in a book by David Owen, where he makes an introduction , it's called "Balkan Odyssey," when he complains about how ignorant certain people were when they discussed the events in the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now tell us what kind of Serbian control was supposed to be established in the Croatian territory, as you included in your report? Or was that an error?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it's an error, it has to be a translation error, Your Honours, because in the first section of part 2, it starts -- which is dedicated to the evolution of the mission and the objectives of the SFRY armed forces during the conflict in Croatia. In the subparagraph d, I write -- and I will only quote part of the paragraph: "The JNA's role has been transformed from one of interposing among the conflicting parties to one of creation and control of Serb-held areas in those parts of Croatia," those parts, I'm sorry, "that the Serb" -- and then between in brackets: "(ian) leadership considers Serb." And I based that on an entry in Kadijevic's book on the English page 0036-2713 when Kadijevic discusses the second stage of the second phase of the operations in Croatian where he says, among other things: "In close coordination with the Serb insurgence, all Serb regions in Croatia, except for a part in Western Slavonia, were liberated. This comprises approximately one-third of the former republic of the Croatia's territory." And he gives more information. But, I mean, for the purposes now, I think this should be sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that that is not sufficient at all. Neither do I think that you explained what I asked you; namely, what was meant by Serbian control in the context of liberating territories in Croatia. But let us move on. My second question: At the time of the conflict in Vukovar, you said that the armed forces of the JNA were duty-bound to apply regulations on the implementation of the international laws of war pursuant to the rules of the service and armed forces of Yugoslavia from 1988. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to address firstly the comment by Mr. Borovic that it was not sufficient. In my book -- in my -- excuse me, in my report I also quote from the book by Borisav Jovic, "Last Days of SFRY," where he also explains the evolution of the Supreme Command and the impact that had on the missions of the JNA. Now, to answer the second part of the question, yesterday I spoke about what is mentioned in section 7 of part 1 of the report, where first quoting from the 1982 All People's Defence law, Article 93, and this is Exhibit 392, the Article says: "During combat activities, members of the armed forces" -- so not just the JNA but also the TO and any other armed people that are admitted into the armed forces -- "are obliged at all times and in all circumstances to abide by the rules of the international law of war on the humane treatment" -- I apologise for the transcript -- "of wounded and captured enemies on the protection of the civilian population and other regulations in this law in compliance with the constitution and the law." We also discussed Article 53 yesterday of the 1985 law on the Serbs in the armed forces. And we discussed the 1988 regulations on the application of international laws of war in the armed forces of the SFRY, which is Exhibit 396, and based on my review of the documents, it's my understanding that all these laws and regulations applied to the situation in Vukovar during October and November 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you went back and quoted Jovic in reply to my previous question, I didn't take it to mean that the transformation of the JNA was such that it grew into a Serbian army. Would you please give us that quotation, if you happen to have it here. If not, then would you please answer my second question. That particular quotation, namely that the JNA, in view of its role, transformed itself into a Serbian army, where does it say that? Or do you not happen to have that quotation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I mean the quotation actually is that at -- and I think I will have to read out from the beginning of the paragraph. It's in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, I haven't got all day. Does it say anywhere in that quotation that the JNA transformed itself into a Serb or Serbian army? Do you have it or not? We're dealing with this one single question already 10 minutes now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Because, Mr. Borovic, you're misunderstanding the answers given by the witness. He hasn't said what you are now putting. And that's why there is delay. You need to listen a little more carefully to what he is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am very attentive, Your Honours, but I did not receive an answer. We shall move on, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So the JNA was duty-bound to apply regulations that you quoted as well as decrees and ratified humanitarian conventions such as The Hague Convention and so on; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. And I would just wish to add briefly that on the pages of the -- 119 to 121 in the second part of the English version, I also discuss a memorandum of understanding that was signed between the parties involved in the conflict and the ICRC, and it's 27th of November, 1991. It was signed. And this is 65 ter number 607, which again reminds --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I apologise, you are deliberately wasting my time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am sorry that I am interrupting the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: But the purpose of my question is not to have you quote all regulations. I accept that portion of your report as an accurate one. I wanted to move on, and my question was quite specific. Yes, all of these conventions, regulations that you quoted applied in the JNA, and I fully agree with you. My question is: Croatian armed and paramilitary formations in the relevant period of time, what were the regulations regulating their activities at the time? Weren't they the regulations from 1988? That was my question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, yesterday it was explained that the aim of my report is to analyse the role and the operations conducted by Operational Group South in October and November 1991. And I also mentioned that my report is not an analysis of the Croatian forces or the -- or the forces operating on the Croatian side. So I'm not able to answer this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, something was not recorded, that those were the regulations of the SFRY from 1988.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, in your report you wrote that the -- that non-Serbs left the TO of Croatia and that it was transformed into Serbian TO. So my question to you is: If the non-Serbs left those institutions and if they did not recognise the SFRY and did not want to be members of the JNA, what would you call it? Would you call it an armed rebellion of non-Serbs at that point in time? And was that a crime, pursuant to the laws in force at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. The question goes beyond the scope of his expertise in military matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think it's fair enough to allow it, Mr. Weiner. Carry on, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am aware of the time constraints, but I think Mr. Borovic didn't quote my report what I wrote in accurate way, because it's discussed on page 27, 28, second part in the English version. I will not quote everything just to save time, but I am right when I talk about local Serb TO. "The local Serb TO in Croatia consists of units created by the local Serbs from the existing TO of the Republic of Croatia in areas where they have a majority or significant minority. In some areas, the existing units of the TO of the Republic of Croatia, due to the conflict, have become de facto Serb," de facto, in italics, "because the non-Serbs have left," and that was what Mr. Borovic read out, "or the non-Serbs do not recognise the SFRY armed forces anymore and cease their cooperation with the JNA." And whether -- what these non-Serbs did is an armed rebellion or not, I mean, that would warrant a separate study because again my report focuses on OG South and the forces operating under the command and control of OG South, and I did not discuss the creation --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Serb armed forces. No, it's not written anywhere. They did not exist at the time. The JNA existed, correct? Namely, that they did not recognise the Yugoslav People's Army. But at any rate, Mr. Theunens, I asked you what these non-Serbs did, did it amount to an armed rebellion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I mean, I can give you two elements of information. As an analyst, I would want to see documents and -- that allow me to study this creation of these forces which, according to Mr. Borovic, carried out an armed rebellion, and based on my knowledge an armed rebellion is a legal concept, so I'm -- I don't think I'm fully qualified to draw a conclusion on that. I think I could analyse the creation of these forces and their structure, organisation, but whether it amounted to an armed rebellion, I think that would be up to somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Do you know, based on which regulations the Croatian paramilitary formations known as ZNG, HOS and Home Guards were established? There are documents confirming that they were established, and also evidence in this trial. Are you aware of this or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, to save time, I will be brief. This report does not study the forces operating on the Croatian side, so therefore I cannot answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Since in the Vukovar TO it was only Serbs who remained, according to you, my question is: Who then violated the then existing Croatian regulations? Was it contrary to the law, the fact that the Serbs and only Serbs remained in the TO of Vukovar? Was that a violation of the then existing laws in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I would object to that again, Your Honour. They are now asking him about violations of Croatian laws.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Technically Mr. Weiner is correct, Mr. Borovic. I have tried to allow you as much scope as possible, but I think you've gone over the edge now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My next question. In your report, Mr. Theunens, you give various claims as to the reasons for establishing operations groups, tactical groups, and assault detachments. In your view what are the basic reasons for establishing these temporary formations, briefly, please? And let me be even more specific. Could the reasons be that, for example, establishment units are not fit to carry out an assignment, could that be a reason rather than what you say, in order to implement subordination and singleness of command? Which would you think takes priority?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Borovic speaks about claims or -- that I give claims in my report. In the first part of the report, English pages 96 to 100, I speak -- I quote from several regulations, SFRY armed forces regulations that define operational groups, tactical groups, assault detachments and assault groups. And they -- these regulations also explain why such ad hoc formations can be established. And I'm just quoting now from a document, 1990 draft doctrine of the Territorial Defence, which is 65 ter 400. It talks about unification of actions of all forces at the battle-field or part of the theatre of war is performed by command of strategic groupings. Strategic groupings are at a higher level than operational groups, but it actually brings me to the answer of the question. Based on my analysis, the operational groups, tactical groups and so on were established to implement or to make sure, excuse me, that the principles of command and control, single authority, unified command and the obligation to implement decisions, are actually applied, and that the function of command and control can be carried out in a smooth manner.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, that's precisely what I asked you. Was that the reason subordination and singleness of command, or was it, in fact, that the establishment units were not fit, were not competent to carry out these assignments. Do you think that it's the former or the latter, or perhaps both of them? Since it is the position of Defence that this other reason, subordination and singleness of command, is not the proper reason, based on the army regulations. This is the position of the Defence. So given that, would you abide by your previous position, or would you accept what we claim; namely, that the establishment units were not fit to carry out the assignment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I answered the question already, Your Honours. Based on my review of the documents available to me, both an extensive collection of SFRY armed forces doctrinal regulations and instructions, as well as specific orders and reports from the 1st Military District and Operational Group South that applied to the October, November 1991 time period, the Operational Group South, in this case, was established to apply the principles of command and control; in particular, because there was such a wide range of different forces participating on the side of the JNA in the operations at the time. I mentioned them already, but we have JNA units, units of the Territorial Defence of Serbia, volunteers, and then units I describe as local Serb TO, which, in fact, were partly affiliated volunteer units. And the Croatian operational group, together with assault detachments and assault groups on the lower echelon, was the most appropriate way to make sure that the principles of command and control could be applied in such a situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is your answer then. My next question: Do you differentiate between the terms "in cooperation" and "in joint action" when it comes to coordination? Would you please tell me whether you see a difference between these two terms?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Coordination, Your Honours, is a function of command and control. It is defined on page 42 in the English version of my report, the first part. Cooperation has no command and control implications. And I quoted from the Exhibit 394 on the pages -- at paragraph 111 to be complete.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question was: Do you know what the term "in joint action" meant within the JNA, and also the term "cooperation," and does "in joint action" mean the organisation within the armed forces, whereas "cooperation" means cooperation between commands and armed forces. Do you see the difference there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding was that in the system of All People's Defence, cooperation referred in first instance to the relations between the JNA and other components or other elements that were involved in All People's Defence, like civil defence or the local civil authorities; whereas, as I explained, coordination is a function of command and control which applies not only within a certain command, for example, within a brigade if two battalions have to carry out an attack, the brigade commander can order these battalions to coordinate in order to make sure that when they advance that there is no gap. Coordination applies certainly in the case when there is fire close air support, from aircraft when there is artillery support and again the coordination is imposed by the commander both within units under his command and as with neighbouring units, for example, which are not under his -- or what I want to say -- because it's unclear. If neighbouring units --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. It's -- it has taken too long. When you say "coordination," do you actually mean "in joint action"? If so, then the matter is closed. I didn't ask you about coordination and cooperation; I asked you about joint action and cooperation. You explained the cooperation properly, and what you are now referring to as coordination, do you actually mean the same thing as joint action? If so, then it's correct.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my review of the doctrinal documentation, coordination does not always imply joint action, but it's -- I would have to check for it. I mean, I have seen joint action, but I haven't seen it always in the context of coordination. I have also seen it in other contexts in JNA regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Or actually, it's time for our break. Let us not move on, but rather move to the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Is a battalion a basic joint unit at the infantry level?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- Your Honours, it's a tactical -- it's yeah, indeed, it's a basic joint unit at the -- no, sorry, I don't understand the question. Because a battalion, a basic joint unit at the infantry level. I mean, there can also be armoured battalions, logistical battalions. Maybe it's a translation thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: My question was: Is a battalion a basic joint tactical unit of the infantry.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand it. You mean an infantry battalion?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: For the third time, yes, indeed, I do mean an infantry battalion. For the third time, I mean the same question that I asked the first time around.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question comes across quite differently in English, Mr. Borovic. But we've got it clear now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Frankly, Your Honours, I can hardly be expected to monitor everything, and we're in a bit of a hurry.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: To cut a long story short, is your answer yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What does the battalion command comprise, or who does it comprise? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It will comprise a commander, like any military unit, and it will also comprise a staff whereby the battalion in the JNA is the first level, when we start from the bottom, that there is a command [realtime transcript read in error "commander"], i.e., a staff included -- I said command, not commander. Where there is a command or a staff that assists the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what a staff comprises? Since you say that a battalion has a staff, who does this staff comprise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, just to bring us back to my report, command structure is discussed on page -- from page 48 of the English version onwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, excuse me. If you go on answering my questions like these, I won't have time to ask you a single question. You said a battalion has a staff. My question is: At the time, at the relevant time, who did the battalion staff comprise? Please don't go back to your report for that. Do you know or do you not know? If you don't know, we can move on.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my testimony here is based on my report, so I think it's -- it's helpful for all of us that I refer to my report. On page 49 of the English version I quote from Exhibit 394, which is the JNA text-book on command and control from 1983, and I will read it out. I say that -- I apologise: "All commands from battalions upwards, are similarly structured. At the head of all commands staffs are commanders who whom all units are directly responsible." And then it continues: "Every command from a regiment upward has its own staff led by a Chief of Staff with at the same time a Deputy Commander." And then in -- I mean, there is more, but I can also refer to --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Excuse me, just a moment. Did you not just read this, that the regiment is the first unit to have a staff and not the battalion? I think part of your report is erroneous in its interpretation of what exactly goes on. Thus I must try to clarify this. A battalion does not have a staff. This starts at a higher level; at least that's our interpretation of the same regulations that you have just referred to. If this was an error that you made, it's not problem at all. We can try to set it right now. Does a battalion have a staff at all, first of all?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From -- I mean, I didn't invent what I just said. I quote from Exhibit 394. And it's on the English pages in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Fine. So it is your submission that a battalion has a staff. Is that your answer?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I hadn't finished my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: This might take seven months, seven years. I'm still asking you the same question. Does a battalion have a staff or not? I think I'm in charge of this cross-examination, not you, Mr. Theunens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm in charge of this courtroom, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the question has been answered. I referred to this quotation from Exhibit 394.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who does the battalion staff comprise then, if that's your answer? Who is it made up of?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the battalion is -- the infantry battalion is -- I'm trying to identify the exhibit in which we -- yeah, it's Exhibit 397, the 1988 JNA battalion manual for the infantry and motorised and so on, battalion. I haven't discussed the battalion staff in detail in my report because I believe that for the purposes of my report studying the brigade staff was more relevant. But if required, I can identify within that regulation how a battalion staff is organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My next question. Are assault detachments established for particular operations at a particular time?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we agree that the fall of Vukovar occurred on the 18th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about after the fall of Vukovar? Was there not a need to set up assault detachments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether the question is -- I mean, the transcript is a correct reflection of the question. Assault detachments based on the documents I reviewed existed prior to the fall of Vukovar. We have requested from Serbia and Montenegro documentation as to -- in relation to orders that were issued to disband assault detachments --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's -- that's fine, Mr. Theunens. You're right. Assault detachments existed until the fall of Vukovar. That was my question. It was very simple. Was there or was there not any need to set up assault detachments after the fall of Vukovar on the 18th of November in a purely military sense? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read in the transcript assault detachments existed until the fall of Vukovar. That is an assumption you make, Mr. Borovic, because the documentation I reviewed does not allow to draw such a conclusion. I -- from the documentation I saw, and we have discussed --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What is your answer to my question? What is your answer to my question? Was there any need after the fall of Vukovar for the existence of assault detachments? What is your answer as a military expert? Was there any need? Did the need exist?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Can you please be so kind as to explain that. Why?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are several -- Your Honours, there are several elements in my reply. First of all, the fact that the operational group continued to exist, Operational Group South continued to exist until at least the 21st -- the 23rd of November, 1991, indicates that the command level right above the assault detachments still needed to exist i.e., that the commander of the command level above the operational group considered it essential to maintain the Operational Group South in its existence. Now, when we look -- second element of reply is the situation. We have discussed a few documents already this morning. Combat operations did not end because of the fall of Vukovar --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sir, excuse me. Just a minute. If that is your continuation, then it's fine. But I didn't ask you about operations groups or tactical groups. All I asked about was assault detachments.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps I have interrupted you. Please accept my apologies. Go on.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's fine. But, I mean, I started with the operational group, why, because the Operational Group South was the command level above the assault detachments. So it wouldn't make sense to have like assault detachments without an operational group above of it. Now, what I was explaining is that based on the documents also that were raised by Mr. Vasic in his cross-examination, there are still resistance pockets or other enemy -- enemies present in Vukovar. I think the document -- the order we discussed on the evacuation of the hospital says that the war is not over. There are also documents; for example, the -- the order by the 1st Military District, Exhibit 415, by General Zivota Panic, where he orders OG South and OG North to seize the hospital. He also, Panic, expresses, his worries about the situation of the Territorial Defence. What I'm trying to say is - and I apologise for the length of the answer - that because of this unstable situation, because of the fact that there are undisciplined elements present, mainly within the TO, it is essential to maintain command and control over these elements at the lowest level possible. That means not only the operational group, but also the levels, command levels below the operational group, and in the context of Operational Group South, that means assault detachments and assault groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, how long am I allowed to go on for exactly? I'm sorry to be asking the question now, but I need a reference point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, the answer is in two parts. The first is strictly 12.30. The more generous one is that you could have 10 further minutes after lunch if you needed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Your Honours. This, I believe, is some sort of a compensation for that one day when I could not. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, an assault detachment, is that a joint tactical unit in attack? Just to complete this, so that you can provide one answer to all my questions, during an attack on a populated area or certain buildings, this is a provisional unit, its composition is provisional, it has armoured vehicles, pioneers, artillery, and a signals component. First of all, is that a correct assessment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours, this comes from Exhibit --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If that's correct, why would there be a need for assault detachments then? What is the populated area that was to be attacked? Which is the joint tactical unit, and after the 18th of November, apart from these pockets that you have referred to, what exactly was going on to call for assault detachments to continue to exist? I would not like to comment on what you said about operations groups or tactical groups, I might perhaps even agree, but assault detachments, provisional ones, used only for special missions, used in order to attack populated areas or fortified facilities. Vukovar fell on the 18th of November; we all know all about that. Why would there continue to be a need for assault detachments, or were these simply disbanded?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, my understanding of reviewing on one hand the doctrinal documents, as has been discussed now, and on the other hand the orders and reports by Operational Group South, indicate that actually assault detachments and assault groups were established to maintain single authority and unified command over all the forces involved, and I mean by this JNA, TO, from the Republic of Serbia, local Serb TO, including volunteers, paramilitaries. As I answered earlier, after the fall of Vukovar this requirement to maintain single authority and unified command of control, still existed. Now, as I mentioned before, I don't have an order that indicates when or whether the assault detachments were disbanded. It was requested from Serbia. If you want I can give the reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that the only need for resubordination and singleness of command was the existence of assault detachment? Was this the sole reason, in your opinion, after the 18th of November?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but, I mean, I want to clarify. Based on what I've seen in other documents, this single authority and unity of command, could also be established by just a subordination order, to say, well, X or Y Territorial Defence is subordinated under that or this battalion. Now, the structure with assault detachments and assault group existed in Vukovar or within Operational Group South prior to the fall of Vukovar. Based on documents I saw, there was no reason to change this structure. If one wanted -- one, i.e. the commander of Operations Group South, wanted to maintain the single authority and the subordination of all forces involved under the JNA. And it should -- I apologise --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Theunens, wouldn't it be simpler for you to simply say yes? I answered [as interpreted] you about the basic reasons for subordination and singleness of command, the basic reason. Why didn't you just answer yes? You're just taking up time. Is your answer yes?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer was given, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on which documents, witness statements, have you established the existence of assault groups in Vukovar, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just trying to locate the order where -- I think it's from the 14th or the -- of November where the commander of OG South, if I remember well, states that a military police battalion has to be -- has to establish assault groups. Yes, this is the -- if I'm not wrong, it's 65 ter number 585. It's the order 403-1 dated the 16th of November, 1991. And it says that the 2nd military police battalion -- battalion, excuse me -- is to make use of assault groups. Now, I think that was not your question. The only additional information I have for assault groups is that I combined the public statement Captain Radic made in an interview. If I remember well, that's Exhibit 3 -- I think it's Exhibit 353, where he said that all -- that he had 500 people in his group, and I linked that up with the doctrine. I tried to find a doctrinal definition for the group of Radic, and assault group would have been then the most logical choice.
