And I apologise again for taking time, but we requested from Serbia and Montenegro all orders issued by Radic or orders received by Radic as well as orders issued by Tesic, so Borivoje Tesic, commander of the 1st Assault Detachment, as well as orders received by Tesic during the 30 September to 23 of November time period that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Excuse me. Do you really have to quote all these documents ad nauseam, if I may put it that way. You simply don't have these documents; that is the simple truth of this matter. My question was based on what did you establish these assault groups, and you say in Miroslav Radic's interview. The long way around, as it were, when he was talking about this group of volunteers, but you did not find a single direct reference to the establishment of any assault groups purely in terms of their establishment. Not in connection with the 1st Assault Detachment or in connection with Miroslav Radic. Yes or no? Do you have a document or a statement to indicate the existence of an assault group?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the statement is the one by Radic, and all I can do from here is to ask Serbia and Montenegro, who is in, my view with the best qualified to provide us with these documents, to provide these documents. If they don't provide the documents or even if they don't do the effort to say, "We don't have them," then it's difficult for me to answer the question. But I think we did sufficient efforts on our side but I think we made sufficient efforts on our side to obtain documents, for example, on how the force in the 1st assault detachment was organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, thank you. Thank you. You didn't have the documents; these are problems of cooperation. I think you are entirely right to point these out, cooperation with the national council; but that is not our topic right now. My next question: Territorial Defence, the detachments, were subordinated to OG South. This is something you said. My question is, do you know how many men a Territorial Defence detachment would have been made up of?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the definition of detachment in the JNA regulations I have seen, a detachment is a unit of variable composition. And that's also something I wish to point out, that because these TO -- I mean Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora, these TO detachments, had no fixed composition; the name "detachment" was used. Now, they were called TO because according to the law everybody who joins the armed forces in defence of the country, but who is not a member of the JNA, will be consisted [sic] a member of the Territorial Defence. Now, whether there is a legal background to this, that's another issue. And if you --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. The composition varies. In view of that, from the point of view of military doctrine, what would be the numerical strength for a TO detachment? Give us a range, please.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only information I have on that comes from the testimony of Witness Trifunovic, and I don't think it's helpful for me repeat it. Again I wish to reiterate, that the TO, i.e. Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora, are only TO by name. Therefore it wouldn't be of assistance to apply theoretical definitions of territorial -- TO -- of TO detachments on formations of the nature of Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Theunens, you are now drawing conclusions, but my question was very specific. Let us leave Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora for later. What about my previous answer [as interpreted], the numerical strength. You are quoting Mr. Trifunovic. Let us trying to jog our member. What number are we talking about, 400 men, 500 men?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, I seem to recall that Trifunovic testified this, could even be more, but what I'm trying to explain, and I will do it now, I will repeat myself, is that the theoretical definition does not necessarily apply to the situation as it was in Vukovar with Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You said yesterday that you did not use any witness statements. You are trying to draw an unbiased conclusion as a military expert. Yet in your previous answer you are trying to draw yet another conclusion. Perhaps we can leave that for the end of our cross-examination. But please answer this question: What about a company, how many men would a company be expected to normally comprise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the first part of your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: How many men can a company have in its composition.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would -- I mean, an infantry company I would assume could be like 150, depends, could be less. It depends of the nature of the infantry company.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What about a detachment? Can a detachment be part of a company in the purely military sense?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It can. Because a detachment, as I indicated earlier, is a unit of variable composition. So you can have a detachment of 10 people, you can have a detachment of 5.000 people, but it won't be wise to have -- obviously it wouldn't make sense to have a detachment of 5.000 people included in a company, whereas a detachment of 10 or 100 people could be included, if the commander of the battalion or the superior command of the company decides to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That's what you suppose. What about specifically? A detachment numbering 500 to 700 people, can it be part of a company numbering 150 people? That's a question for a military expert.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, Your Honours. But, I mean, such a purely theoretical question, whereby we come with numbers, I don't know what they're based on. I don't think it's helpful for me to answer such a question, because I think the reply may be misleading and highly incorrect. It's easy to challenge a reply to such a question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever hold in your hands the manual of the JNA on infantry battalions from 1988?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, Your Honours. And if I remember well, it's Exhibit 397.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you find there that an assault group may have the strength equivalent to a reinforced platoon and that it is not written anywhere that an assault group may be a reinforced company? Would you agree with me? This is a theoretical question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. And this is explained in paragraph 26 of Exhibit 397 on page 99 of my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on the rules in force in the JNA, does a company have a staff or not? I think that you explained this in relation to a battalion and regiment, but now I'd like to hear your explicit answer as to whether a company has a staff or not. Or is it only at the levels above that a staff is created?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the JNA regulations I reviewed, a company does not have a staff, but the company commander will be assisted by certain people who will do certain aspects of work that could be considered as staff work. But it's not a staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 57 of the third section, you say that the 1st Assault Detachment had three assault groups: Leva Supoderica, Petrova Gora, and another one, and Vukovar. According to the rules, what is the strength of assault groups within a battalion? We heard just a little bit ago that it was a reinforced platoon. Can you then explain to us this claim of yours that the 1st Assault Detachment had three assault groups: Petrova Gora, Leva Supoderica, and Vukovar. First of all, is this written in your report or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there must be a translation error, because on page 57 in the second part of the report in the paragraph g -- I will not read out the whole paragraph but just the two relevant sentences which is actually the summary of what follows in this section 3. It says: "The 1st Assault Detachment consists of three assaults groups, full stop. The Petrova Gora, Leva Supoderica (commanded by Milan Lancuzanin, also known as Kameni), and Vukovar (commanded by Miroljub Vujovic), (local Serb) TO detachments are subordinated to OG South through the 1st Assault Detachment." So these are two different sentences, and there is no link whatsoever in this text between the three assault groups and the names of the local Serb TO units that follow. So maybe something went wrong with the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. All right, Mr. Theunens. I think that you understood properly my question. According to the rules of battalion of company and of platoon, what is the main means of communication when attacking a settlement? Is it, for example, radio communication?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Radio communication would be one of the means of communication that can be used. However, there are also other means that can be used like signs, a courier. Yes, and this is purely theoretical answer I give because I don't have that regulation or that particular paragraph of the regulation in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What about when attacking a settlement? Is then a radio link the main means of communication, and does it reduce the need to use couriers? There are streets, we're talking of a settlement. The attack proceeds street by street. Do you know this? It's not terribly important.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have the regulation in front of me, but from my own experience I know, and maybe it had to do with our radios, that in built-up areas, because, for example, there are higher buildings and there is metal that can be integrated in the concrete structures, that it's sometimes difficult to use radios actually, and therefore, because of poor communications, and therefore other means, like if you are at short distance you use signs or a courier can be more effective. But I'm willing to look at the regulation if you show it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In order not to waste time there are smaller houses, larger houses, but it seems that we are now in the domain of imposation [as interpreted], both you and me. Let us move on. You quoted the interview given by Radic where he said, "I am sickened by the war." It's page 83 in the third chapter of your report. This is the text where he claims to have had about 500 people, 500 men. Is that the interview you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours, it's Exhibit 353. Now, I mean, Radic -- you say Radic claims. I would assume that an officer before he speaks to the media has received an authorisation to do so and is also aware of the implication of the things he says to media. That's the system and the situation in my military, and I assume it was the same in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the moment when the combat operations were in the final stage, were being concluded, I don't think that there was a need -- or I'm not sure that there was a need for anyone to ask for a special authorisation, especially not in Vukovar. But that's not important. What is important is just a minute ago you confirmed that Trifunovic testified in the case and that when it comes to the composition of TO detachment, it is in his evidence that you found support for your position. My question is: If the 80th Kragujevac Motorised Brigade in that axis had a battalion numbering 400 people, which is what Vukosavljevic, Chief of Staff of security of the Kragujevac Brigade testified about, and it pertains to the same period of time referred to by Radic when speaking of assault groups, can we then agree that this is a case where a journalist interprets what constituted this group, even if he conveyed Radic's words, because in the military sense Radic could not have been the commander of a battalion of the 80th Kragujevac Motorised Brigade, and it was positioned in the same axis, in same location in Petrova Gora where Radic was. So do you believe that a statement given to the papers and the interpretation that was given could not be used by you as a military expert in order to draw a conclusion that he had 500 people under his command?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are several components in this question. As I said earlier, this report is limited to -- I mean, the sources of the report are limited to document -- to official documentation, SFRY legislation, 1st Military District, OG South, and SSNO orders and reports, as well as some open sources. Now, I wish to comment on what Mr. Borovic said in relation to Trifunovic. My understanding of the testimony of Trifunovic is that he provided a theoretical answer to a theoretical question in relation to TO detachments. I'm a bit confused by the reference that is made to Vukosavljevic. I just wish to say that it's not me who concluded that there was 500 people in Radic's unit. It is a quotation from the interview. Now if the journalist misunderstood him, then I would have expected Radic to complain with the newspaper and to ask for a clarification. It happens every day. Now, I'm not aware of such a clarification or a rectification. And when I say it happens every day, everyday in the newspapers you see that there are rectifications to certain articles. And, again, I wish to emphasise that based on my understanding of the JNA, interviews can only be given with the authorisation of superiors, and I would assume that these superiors would also screen the nature of the replies because there could be, for example, implications on security aspect --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I think you've already said that. Once again, you are taking too much time. My question is: A reinforced platoon of a company comprising an assault group, can it number 500 people?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier when discussing the assault detachment, Your Honours, based on my review of the documents, it is my -- my conclusion that the terms "assault detachment" and "assault groups" were used for formations which were, in fact, i.e., in practice, bigger than the formations as they were envisaged in the doctrine. But the concept behind it is the same, it's only the size that is different. And this is reinforced by what Radic said in this media interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I didn't understand in the end. How many people can a reinforced platoon within an assault group have? And if that is the case, then how many people can an assault detachment have, both from the point of view of the military doctrine and practical matters? Can an assault group be 500-men strong? And if so, then how many men can an assault detachment have?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think I answered the question. Based on the documents I saw in relation --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you. Thank you. On page 86 of the English version of your report, third part of it, here under paragraph 19 and 20 you mention orders dated 14th and 16th November, 1991; correct? First let's clarify that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is -- Could we put Exhibit 405 on our screens, please? This is an order for blockade and attack dated the 1st of October, 1991. You're familiar with this, right? In paragraph 2 it says -- it says: "Motorised guards brigade shall put under blockade and attack Vukovar within the operative group by using assault detachment." And then: "In joint action with Vukovar TO units (Petrova Gora detachment) armoured battalion of the 544th Motorised Brigade, defeat enemy forces in the area of operations, take control of that part of town and establish control, law and order." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. But, I mean, if you want to see it on the screen, you have to go to the paragraph 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Would you be so kind and look at paragraph 5 of this same order? Does it say there: "Tasks of units." Paragraph 5 under 1. "The 1st Assault Detachment comprising 1st Motorised Brigade with 3-1 armoured battalion, 2-2 LSARD," and then "1-3/2 military police battalion, and pioneer squad, detachment commander of 1st Motorised Brigade commander," and so on. They also use guides from Petrova Gora TO detachment. Is that what it says here, Mr. Theunens, and is it clear to you?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This -- this is indeed what this order of 1st of October says.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The 1st Assault Detachment at that time, was it under command of Major Borivoje Tesic? Have you come across such information? Commander of the 1st Battalion and commander of the Assault Detachment 1.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this order, Your Honours, the 1st of October order, it says in this paragraph 5 that the detachment commander will be the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion. And I know from -- I think these were articles that were published in Narodna Armija on the guards brigade that Tesic was indeed the commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion. So I can only assume that there was no change in -- in -- in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You're fully correct. Now, could we please see Exhibit 408? This is the decision of the commander of the OG South dated 15th of October, 1991. Do you see paragraph 2, Mr. Theunens? I will read this out so as to spare you. "Tasks for units." So this is the 15th of October, 1991: "(a) Assault Detachment 1 comprising 1st Motorised Battalion. 3-1 company/armoured battalion. 1-2 company platoon of the military police battalion, and one company of volunteers from the current deployment continue the attack and in joint action with Assault Detachment 2 and 3/211 of the armoured brigade and Petrova Gora units, crush the Ustasha units on the directions ..." And then it lists the directions, right, or axis, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now see Exhibit 410? Once again here, Mr. Theunens, this is a decision of the commander of the OG South. 29th October 1991 is the date. All right. We have tasks given to units, and it says under 1: "1st Assault Detachment comprising 1st Motorised Battalion, 1, 2, 3 battalion of the military police, detachment Leva Supoderica, Petrova Gora detachment, company of volunteers from Novi Sad, one tank M-84." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. So that means that Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora are subordinate units of the 1st Assault Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: At that time was Borivoje Tesic commander of the 1st Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the documents I have seen, I cannot draw such a conclusion, but I know from witness statements that Borivoje Tesic, and also from testimony I know that Borivoje Tesic was then the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment. Sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Based on all the information available to you, all the documents that you have read, who then was responsible to the OG South for the use of TO detachments and Leva Supoderica detachment? Based on everything we have read so far.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obvious -- I mean, these are orders from the brigade level -- from the operational group level, I'm sorry. Operational group issues orders to the assault detachments. Now, it would not be coherent with the principles of command and control that the operational group would order the assault detachment commander how to organise his forces, i.e., whether he would set up assault groups or not. Maybe it's real possible that the operational group commander ordered the assault detachment commander to organise his forces in assault groups, but it would be unusual for the operational group level, or call it the brigade level, to tell the assault detachment, or call it battalion level, how to organise its companies, if I could compare the assault groups to companies. I'm just trying to explain how the chain of command would work. So these documents do not allow to draw a conclusion on that level. We would the orders the commander of the assault detachment has issued during October and November in order to be able to answer your question, Mr. Borivoje -- Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. But we can agree, can't we, that talking of these tasks it was within the 1st Assault Detachment that the TO detachments were used as well as Leva Supoderica detachments, so does this mean that the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment is responsible to the OG South command for their use? That is my question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah, as long as they're subordinated to him, as it is explained in this order. He is responsible for their use. To the commander of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I apologise for overlapping, I thought that you concluded your answer. Could we see Exhibit 431 on our screens, please. This is the decision of the commander of the OG South dated 16th November 1991. Let us now look at paragraph 2, item 1 within it. Once again, these are tasks given to units. Does it say under item 1: "1st Motorised Battalion in line with the task given on the 14th of November 1991," Mr. Theunens, what we read previously, "with the support of part of the forces of the armoured battalion of the Guards Motorised Brigade ought to continue the attack on the axis Sundarciceva Street-Rade Koncara settlement - bridges over the Vuka River ..." and so on and so on. Does it say here that the 1st Motorised Brigade has tasks which are in line with the task given on the 14th of November, 1991? Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now let us go back to Exhibit 430, which is the decision on the 14th of November, 1991 that we didn't quote previously. So it's Exhibit 430. In that order, Exhibit 430, 14th of November, 1991, under item 2 we see "tasks for units," and then subitem 4, does it say there the 1st Assault Detachment (minus the 1 Motorised Battalion) from the current sector of the combat disposition is to be moved to axis of Dalmatinska Street-Alije Alijagica-another street, water-tower. So it's paragraph 2, item 4, does it say that there? Have you found that, Mr. Theunens? We have tasks for the units, paragraph 2, and then underneath it we see item 4. That is to say, 1, 2, 3, 4.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In paragraph 4, it speaks about the 1st Assault Detachment minus the 1st Motorised Battalion. And then later on in paragraph 5 the mission or the task of the 1st Motorised Battalion is explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Can we agree, then, that this order dated 14th of November, 1991 states that the 1st Assault Detachment now functions without the 1st Motorised Battalion but together with other units comprising it, right? At least that was explained by General Trifunovic; you were present then. Is that your position as well? Or rather, is that what is stated here?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that Trifunovic made it to general, but that's another thing, even though I appreciate him a lot. I think what this order says, that it's up to the commander, i.e., the operational group commander to decide how he organises his forces. In this order the commander of Operational Group South decided, based on his planning for the operations for the following day, which he in his term, based on the -- the taskings or the assignment he had received from the commander of the 1st Military District, he decided to rearrange his forces and to take out -- take the 1st Motorised Battalion out of the 1st Assault Detachment for at least that day, for this specific operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Theunens. Would it then be a fair conclusion on the part of the Defence that Major Tesic continues to be commander of the 1st Motorised Battalion and the 1st Assault Detachment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unless there was another order that would specify or that would give additional instructions on that level, it would be a correct assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us go back to Exhibit 431, please. We had it on our screens a while ago. This is the decision of the commander of OG South dated the 16th of November, 1991. I showed you in all fairness what the situation was on the 14th of November. Could we then agree that what this exhibit demonstrates -- 431. The 1st Motorised Battalion -- just a minute, please. 431. This is what I read out to you a while ago. It says: "Tasks. The 1st Motorised Battalion, in line with the task given on the 14th of November, 1991," and then it describes the axis and the tasks given or assigned. Isn't that what it says, the order dated the 14th of November? And there is another one dated the 16th of November. The one dated the 16th of November is the one you've looked at and it's in keeping with the one dated the 14th of November. Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, that's referred -- that's the reference in the first sentence of paragraph 2, "tasks by the units."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So would you be so kind as to tell us right now at this precise time when talking about the order dated the 16th of November, under whose command were the Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora TO detachments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order does not allow to draw a conclusion on that. However, there is a report, 407-1, which, if I'm correct, is the Exhibit 414, lists, among the losses, members of the Petrova Gora and Vukovar TO. I should have said report 407-1 of OG South, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. Theunens, but that's not what I had in mind. My question is about this: Three companies of the 1st Motorised Battalion were taken to a different axis, whereas the 1st Assault Detachment remained along a -- an altogether different axis, that it no longer has the battalion within its compositions, then my question is very simple. Members of the Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora detachments who stayed with the 1st Assault Detachment at this point in time, under whose command would they be? Would they be under the command of the commander of the 1st Assault Detachment? That's my question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the two orders we have seen, the one for the 14th of November and one for the 16th of November, do not mention Leva Supoderica or Petrova Gora. So maybe it's an omission, maybe there is an operational plan behind it. From these two orders, I cannot draw any conclusion as to whether Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora stayed within the 1st Assault Detachment or were maybe fully incorporated in the 1st Motorised Battalion. So, yeah, there would be a requirement for additional information reports or orders from that time period in order to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that is precisely why I was taking one step at a time. All these orders from October were the first thing I showed you, and then we talked about the composition of the 1st Assault Detachment, and then I reached the 16th and the 14th. The assault detachment keeps its previous composition with the exception of the 16 of November, the date that I mentioned. This is when the 1st Motorised Battalion was taken away from it, separated from it. That is why there is no reference to them. Why, because they're part of the 1st Assault Detachment. Still there is no change in the composition except on the 16th of November, the 1st Motorised Battalion being taken outside the 1st Assault Detachment, the only change that occurs over this time, the composition remains the same. There is this one staying behind, nothing changes. More specifically, in addition to all these documents that I've quoted to you now, have you ever found another document dealing with orders given by Operations Group South after the 16th of November, something that could have changed this situation, or have you found nothing? Once again, because this is my last question for this session and then just briefly after the break, I quoted October, the composition of the 1st Assault Detachment. I specified who Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora belonged to, the TO detachments, what their assignments were. I quoted the order dated the 14th, their composition. And then finally the 16th with the 1st Motorised Battalion being taken outside its unit and the two detachments remained within the 1st Assault Detachment. There is not a single order or document to show that they left their original composition, which would have been logical, after all, but they stayed within the 1st Assault Detachment. Would I be right in saying this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I answer -- as I already mentioned to the previous question, these orders show the situation as it is on the 14th and the 16th of November, and they -- of November, 1991. And they indeed -- they -- in the one for the 14th of November, they give different assignments to the 1st Assault Detachment than to the 1st Motorised Battalion. However, it would be helpful to have orders for the 17th and the 18th of November in order to establish the composition not only of -- of the 1st Assault Detachment or the 1st Motorised Battalion, but also to see what the mission or the task of the subordinate forces, including the local Serb TO was. You see, in my report that all I can conclude on that level is that on the 21st of November at 6.00 in the morning, 21st of November, 1991, Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica are still subordinated to OG South. Now, I will not repeat that we have requested these documents, but indeed we have requested for missing documents, and it's easy to establish the documents which are missing because they all have a number. And so far Serbia and Montenegro has not provided these documents. So that is one of the -- that's the main reason why I cannot answer the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, the 21st, resubordination and everything else, my learned friends will be asking you about that, I have no time. But that's why I'm asking you if you have found any document relating to after the 16th of November, something that you found that would indicate a change in the situation in terms of respective responsibilities, with the exception of the 21st of November in relation to Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica TO detachments, or were they still within the composition of the 1st Assault Detachment with the 1st Motorised Battalion with all its companies missing now? Have you found any document to depict this situation differently? That is my question, and not in a more general sense what became of the TO, as far as the -- as far as OG South was concerned.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether I found or didn't find such a document is -- is of limited relevance. I didn't find such a document, but it can partly be explained by the fact that there are documents we have requested, we didn't obtain, but didn't obtain. So maybe the documents that are still missing would assist in answering your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there is no such document, needless to say, since of course you haven't found it, could we then agree that on the 16th of November, 1991 members of the Territorial Defence detachments, Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora, were under the command of the 1st Assault Detachment whose commander at the time was Borivoje Tesic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the two orders we have been discussing now, the 14th of November one and the 16th of November one, do not allow to draw such a conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What conclusion then can you draw for us? Under whose control could they possibly have been, if you look at these orders after the 16th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we know -- what we know from these orders is as follows: We know that the commander of the -- excuse me, the commander of Operational Group South changes the composition of its subordinate units probably based on the operational requirements which are as a result of the assignment he has received from his commander, i.e., the commander of the 1st Military District. As I said, we don't have any orders by the 1st Assault Detachment, so it is difficult -- I mean, that's why I didn't draw any conclusions on how the 1st Assault Detachment was organised. I can only say which forces are included in the 1st Assault Detachment, but I don't know from the documents how these forces are organised. Radic interview, Exhibit 353 is the only documentary evidence of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I don't think that has anything to do with my question. Nothing to do with it the question. Thank you. Mr. Theunens, that's your answer. That's fine. Your answer is fine. Exhibit 374, it's an order dated the 9th of November, 1991. Mr. Vasic told you about this one. This is about the appointment of local commanders. You've looked at that one, I assume. My question is about Exhibit 418. Can we please have that on our screens? Mr. Theunens, this is a regular combat report. In this regular combat report it says that pursuant to order 349-1, and that's the order from Exhibit 374, General Mrksic appointed the following men as local commanders, and you confirmed this yesterday. In Negoslavci, Ljubisa Vukasinovic. In Berak village, Glusevic. In Ovcara village, Jakubovac and Grabovo, Lieutenant-Colonel Slobodan Misovic. When he left the OG South area of responsibility, Lieutenant-Colonel Milorad Vojnovic was appointed. Item 4, after Vukovar was liberated, the following men were appointed commanders in Vukovar: For Vucedol and Mitnica, Major Stupar. And what I wish to ask you about now, for Petrova Gora and the western section between the graveyard and the Vuka River, Major Borivoje Tesic. Isn't that what the report says? This report refers to the order that I have just quoted. Isn't that what it says?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that not mean that the Petrova Gora local commander on the 20th of November, at least as far as these documents seem to suggest, Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica, these detachments, were in his area of responsibility. Was this not, in fact, Major Borivoje Tesic? Was he not, in fact, the local Petrova Gora commander at the time? Isn't that what it means?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have explained yesterday that town commanders, or local commanders is one aspect. Operational commanders is another aspect. A town commander has, as I explained, duties which relate to the exercising of not civilian but military authority and administration; whereas an operational commander has operational duties. Now, of course from the point of view of the command of Operational Group South, to whom all these town commanders are subordinated, it makes sense to appoint as town commanders in the various zones of responsibility within his zone of responsibility a commander who is also an operational commander in that area. So because it would be confusing to appoint somebody else to be responsible for certain aspects of -- of life, or in the zone of responsibility where there is already an operational commander, it would make more sense to install these two authorities in one person.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be right, what I asked you a while ago, about the 20th of November, Borivoje Tesic was the Petrova Gora local commander, and as such the commander of the area where the Vukovar TO and Leva Supoderica TO detachments were stationed? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to be difficult, but it says that Tesic is appointed town commander for Petrova Gora. Now, I have no document in front of me which shows where Leva Supoderica or Petrova Gora are on the 20th of November, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, do you know how these two detachments got their names, Petrova Gora and Leva Supoderica? What if I told you that these were the names of their respective places, Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora? And the entire area is usually described as Petrova Gora. Would that perhaps assist you in giving an affirmative answer to my question? That's where their headquarters was too. That's what my information is based on, and that's what my question is based on. My second but last question. I have 20 seconds left. Please tell us yes or no, so that I can ask you another final question.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I know how these detachments got their names, but this document does not say what they were doing or where they were on the 20th. It cannot be ruled out that they were ordered to operate somewhere else in another part of Vukovar. Maybe it wouldn't make such sense, I agree with you, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, thank you. Fine, thank you. We'll leave it up to the Chamber to draw all the conclusions. Mr. Theunens, have you ever spoken to Witness Radoje Paunovic?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I was involved in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever spoken to a witness called Borivoje Tesic? Have you ever spoken to Major Vukasinovic, Witness Major Vukasinovic? Are you familiar with his evidence?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have spoken to Major -- or at the time Borivoje Tesic. I was not involved in the interview of Major Vukasinovic, but I read his -- the statement -- the statement he provided to the OTP as well as his testimony in the various trials in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, you stated yesterday that you are interested in justice being done, regardless of the fact that you are an employee of the OTP. You say it was based on your suggestion that the OTP decided to amend the indictment in the best interests of justice. Therefore, my last question to you: Did you perhaps make any suggestions for these witnesses or their evidence never to appear in court? I would also like to thank the Trial Chamber for granting me so much time. This is my final question. Please answer, sir.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. But, I mean, I want to -- I need to point out that you are misquoting me. I didn't make any suggestions to amend indictments. When Mr. Vasic asked his question yesterday to me, he was asking whether I was involved in amending indictments, and indeed I was involved because, why, the legal team asked me to review the military terminology that was used. So I think if you want to quote my testimony, you have to do it in accurate way, because otherwise we lose time, as we do now. Now, to answer the question, there have been discussions in the trial team as to whether who should appear as a witness and who not. A trial team consists of several people. It's an -- it's not a military unit, I mean, even though there is one boss, or one leader, opinions are being exchanged, and various constraints, including time constraints, are also highlighted, and then a decision is taken as to whether person X or Y will be called as a witness or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: I have concluded. This was my last question. All I would like to say to you, sir, is I'm not even allowed to hint at what these witnesses actually said, but if those witnesses had been allowed to appear, a lot of the charges against my client would have to be dropped. It's as simple as that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic, how can you put that as a question to this witness? You know that's beyond his capacity. That was a purely hypothetical suggestion on your part at this point. Whether you will have evidence to support that proposition at the end of the trial remains a different matter. Thank you, Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're quite right, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will now adjourn for the break. In view of the fact that Mr. Borovic was allowed to run over to finish the theme of his questioning, we will resume a little late, at five minutes to 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.43 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Judge Thelin is not sitting at the moment. It may be that he will be able to join us again later in the afternoon. We hope so. We will continue to sit in accordance with the Rule in the meantime. Mr. Lukic. Oh, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. Good afternoon to all.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Theunens. I am Momcilo Bulatovic, one of Mr. Sljivancanin's Defence counsel. I will be asking questions on behalf of our team. You've been asked this before - we don't have much time, the time constraints are quite great - whenever you can, please provide brief answers. If there is any need for further clarifications, we will be happy to accommodate you. Today and yesterday you spoke about the operations group, and you told us what an operations group is, or should be. What I want to know is: An operations group as a provisional, temporary unit, does it have a designated area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, based on my review of JNA doctrinal documentation, an operational group, like any other unit, will have a zone of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We heard about the composition of an operations group. What I want to know about is what about the unit which comprise an operations groups, do these units have their own respective areas or zones?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Each -- I mean, the operations group consists of other units. These units have been discussed earlier, and each of these units which have a zone of responsibility, and altogether these zones of responsibility make up or make the -- or constitute the zone of responsibility of the operational group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that on the 20th of November, 1991, within the composition of Operations Group South, one of the units was the 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the -- on documentation of Operations Group South, both orders and reports, I would agree with that assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me whether, while writing your report, you obtained information perhaps -- or can you perhaps simply tell us which is exactly the area that was covered by the 80th Motorised Brigade? Which specific area was that at the time on the 20th of November, 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, we would have to look at the specific orders for that day, and in these orders the zone of responsibility of the 80th Motorised Brigade for that day would be -- will be specified.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does that mean that right now you -- you are unable to answer that question, sir?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the report is based on documents, so I think it would be logical if you ask a question about a specific zone of operations on a specific day, that we look at the order and then see together what the zone of responsibility was as it was specified in that order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We won't be going into that. That's a bit too comprehensive for our purposes and we may end up losing a lot of time, of which we only have a very little. Who makes the decision to appoint someone commander of an operations group? Whose call is that?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is up to a superior commander. Now, as we discussed this morning, there are examples where the commanders of operational -- of operations groups elsewhere in Croatia were appointed by the commanders of the military districts in that area, or military district in that area. I do not have an order appointing Colonel Mrksic to the position of commander of Operations Group South, so I do not know from the military documentation who appointed Mrksic to that position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, sir: This decision of the relevant command - relevant for appointing an operations group commander, I mean - does this decision have to be in writing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first part of my report I discuss command documents, and command documents can be divided in two categories, i.e., orders and reports. And for the orders there are different levels. You have directives, instructions, orders and commands, and according to the definitions of these various categories of call it orders, important matters have to be ordered via a written order. So I would assume, based on those definitions, that it should be done through a written order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I'm led by your answer to assume that this was of paramount importance, it would have called for a written order, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. And just to complete my previous answer, this is explained in pages 57, 58 and 59 of my report in the English version, first part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What about the decision to set up an operations group? What about that sort of decision, does this have to be in writing?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I mentioned earlier, I mean, important matters should be ordered through a written order, so actually in this case, I mean for the establishment of operations group, there should also be a written order. And I can add, I mean, I have -- I'm repeating myself. We have requested these orders as well as others from Serbia and Montenegro over the past years, but we have not obtained a reply. So we don't even know whether there is an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Within the framework of the same set of questions we heard that an operations group has a commander. What about the decision to appoint this commander, which seems to be an important issue too, would that not have to be in a written form as well?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you have asked this question before. This is the question prior to your last question, so -- and I provide an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I think maybe it was a question of poor interpretation. I was asking about the command of an operations group. And now I'm talking about the commander as the top level of the command itself, in a manner of speaking.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say it can be summarised when an operations group is established a commander will be appointed as well as a command. And there may be additional orders in case other officers have to be transferred to that command, i.e., to become a member of the staff, if I can express it that way. But the order to establish the operational group will also include, at least based on what I have seen for other areas, the name of the commander, as well as the unit on which the operation group is based, as well as the other units that are included in the operational group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your report, you mentioned a number of operations groups. These operations groups that you mentioned in your report, did you ever see any order to set up any of these?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. On page 54, English version, part 2, I talk about the strictly confidential order number 09/75-1034, which is issued by the 5th Military District command of the JNA to establish the 3rd Operational Group, and we're talking now about the area south of Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What does this order to set up this operations group contain? What are the elements? Is this something you're familiar with?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't included this specific order in -- in full in my report, but I have included the following information, page 54. So according to this order of the 5th Military District command, OG 3 will be commanded by Lieutenant-Colonel General Vladimir Banjanin and will operate under the direct command of the 5th Military District. Now, I mean, we could show the document, if you want. It should be 65 ter 433, and I'm not sure whether it's in this document, but related orders for the operations in western Croatia, orders for operational groups and tactical groups also included an overview of the units that were included in those operational groups or tactical groups. And I refer, for example, to Tactical Group 2 in my report on the same page, which was tasked with the attacks on the Saborsko area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You are a military analyst. You deal with these sorts of issues. You mention this order, so let me ask you this: In your view, an order establishing an operations group, what kind of elements must it contain?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought I mentioned it, but I -- if -- I mean, maybe I wasn't clear. The order should -- based again on the other orders I have seen, the orders I've seen for other operational groups should include the name of the commander, the name of the superior, a description of the zone of responsibility or at least the initial tasking of the operational group, as well as the units that are included in the operational group. In addition, I have seen also orders for the establishment of operational groups where the -- I would call the most important unit of the operational group is -- is defined in order to determine which command will form the command of the operational group. Now, I'm familiar also -- I mean, to be entirely complete, there was an Operational Group 2 active in the Dubrovnik area in the latter half of 1991 and early half of 1992. And there I think that, if I remember well, for example, the commander was appointed from a different area or from a different unit than the units that should have been or that were initially involved originally in Dubrovnik. That's just a detail to complete the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Theunens, let me ask you this: This order on the establishment of an operations group, I'm not talking about a specific order, just an order, since we have beyond dispute that this was an ad hoc formation, established in order to carry out an assignment, the order establishing this operations group, should it also contain the description of the assignment for the implementation of which an operations group is established?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, I mentioned that. Now, ad hoc doesn't mean it has to be disbanded the day after. It could be, or it's well possible based on the documents I've seen that an assignment is so large that it will take several weeks or even several months to carry out that assignment. And as long as the superior commander considers that it is necessary to maintain the existence of the operational group, it will exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I think that we can agree, you and I, that an operations group as an ad hoc formation, is established for the purposes of a specific assignment, right?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would be correct in theory, but again from the documents I've seen it is well possible that the authority or the commander that established that order to establish the operational group changes the assignment over time, or -- yeah, or amends it or maybe gives additional assignments. What is important, I think, in this context, is that operational structures, even if they're ad hoc, they should only be changed if they are operational requirements to do so, because each time you change the organisation, each time it's actually -- it becomes complicated during a certain time period to implement command and control, or at least to have that command, the operational group function.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If we have a situation where a commander or the command of the operations group amends the assignment that was initially given by those establishing an operations group, do they have to inform the command, the superior command, which established this operations group in writing about these changes, and the reasons for them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe I wasn't a hundred per cent clear in my previous answer, but if there is -- if there are any changes to the assignment it cannot be done by the operational group commander on his own initiative. He basically does what his superior tells him, so it's his superior that will change if there is requirement to do so, that will change the assignment. And in the cases I've seen it's actually the same authority, I mean if there was a change in the assignment it was done by the same authority as the one that had established, or that ordered to establish the operational group. So somebody who is superior to the commander of the operational group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You analysed the documents that were available to you, that were disclosed to you, documents relating to OG South. So please tell me: Did you find anywhere anything indicating that the initial assignment of the OG South was amended, and if so, who and when issued a decision on this?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I've explained before, we don't have the order that established Operational Group South, so it's difficult then to -- to assume whether there were any changes to the initial assignment as it was described or put in this initial order to establish Operational Group South or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke of areas of responsibility of establishment unit, which are within the operations group. Let me ask you this: Changes in the area of responsibility of establishment units, or changes in the area of responsibility of the operations group, do they mean an amendment of the initial assignment?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, it's difficult to answer this question, because it's -- it all depends of the assignment. If the assignment is to capture or to defend a certain zone of responsibility, then it's obvious that the change in the zone of responsibility will probably be the result of the fact that there has been a change in the assignment. Now, I can imagine that there are other changes in assignment which may not affect the zone of responsibility, and vice versa, but it's a very theoretical question. But, I mean, the zone of responsibility is a result of the assignment. It's not the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Establishment units as a whole, do they fall within the operations group comprising them?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether I understand the question, Your Honours. But the documentation I reviewed in relation to operational groups, both on the doctrinal level as well as the orders for operational groups in the various parts of Croatia, indicate that all units that are present in the zone of responsibility of an operations group are subordinated to that operations group.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I just asked you whether they are taken as a whole. For example, if we have a battalion, does the battalion as a whole become a part of the operations group, or only its component parts do? Or let me give you a specific example. The 80th Motorised Brigade, did it in its entirety become a component of the OG South or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, based on the documents I reviewed, the 80th Brigade in its entirety became a component of OG South. But it could be imagined that -- and for whatever reason the commander thinks he needs to order such a change, that when subordinating the 80th Brigade to OG South, the commander who issued that order, he could also have taken elements of the 80th Brigade out of the composition of the 80th Brigade and subordinated it to another command level; for example, Operational Group North. But that would be done for specific operational requirements. And as I said, all elements of the 80th Brigade that were present, that were deployed within the zone of responsibility of OG South, were under the command of the commander of OG South. Like any other unit within the zone of responsibility of OG South.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when writing your report did you see any order, written order, or did you find any evidence supporting that -- the claim that Veselin Sljivancanin was appointing security commander of the OG South?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe it's a translation issue, but "security commander," I assume you mean chief of the security organs or assistant commander for security.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I meant he was appointed chief of the security organ of the OG South.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. Now, it is correct that I don't have a document signed by Sljivancanin as chief of the security organs of OG South. The one document we obtained on the 18th of May, 2006 says Guards Motorised Brigade, or chief of security organs, Guards Motorised Brigade. Now, from all the documentation I reviewed for Operational Group South, as well as the war diary of the Guards Motorised Brigade, it is clear that the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade takes over the command of OG South, which includes that Major Sljivancanin, as chief of the security organs, or assistant commander for security of the Guards Motorised Brigade, becomes chief of the security organs or assistant commander for security for Operational Group South.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. You suppose this. But you have no written document to support this. Let me ask you this: Have you ever seen any document sent by my client, Mr. Sljivancanin, to the relevant authorities, those he was duty-bound to inform, where he signed his name as chief of security of the OG South? Or have you ever seen a document or any kind of an order sent to him in his capacity as chief of the security organ within the OG South?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I may have mentioned that before, but over the past four -- no, over the past three and a half years at least four requests were sent to Serbia and Montenegro to request documents that are related to Major Sljivancanin, both in his position as command -- as chief of the security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade, as well as chief of security organs of OG South. And the only document we obtained so far was the one I just mentioned, i.e., the document obtained on 18th of May, 2006, which is even unsigned whereby Sljivancanin under his name has the indication that he is chief of the security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade. The reason why I mentioned this is that from the neighbouring unit of Operations Group South, i.e., the units that were present in other parts of Eastern Slavonia and Baranja, we have for the month of October at least four reports that were drafted by security organs on the situation with an individual under the nickname Arkan, and these reports are included -- these documents are referred to in my report in the second part.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, it doesn't matter to me at all. I saw those four reports of yours about Arkan. I was just interested in this, you said you never saw anything of the sort, so let us move on. A unit which became a component of an operations group has a security organ, and does this security organ continue to function as a security organ of that establishment unit?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, unless there are orders to the contrary.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever come across an order where the security organs of units, within the OG South, were ordered otherwise?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, can you tell me what are the counter-intelligence tasks carried out by a security organ within an establishment unit, say motorised guards brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I will quote this from the regulation, which is explained on page 78, first part of the English version of my report, and this regulation corresponds with Exhibit 107. It's the rules of service of the security organs in the armed forces of SFRY. And in paragraph 1: "The counter-intelligence task is described as detecting and preventing activities aimed at subverting or disrupting the social order established by the constitution of the SFRY and threatening the country's security if such an activity is carried out in the armed forces or against the armed forces from within the country or from abroad." So it has to do with discovering and counting the internal/external enemy in SFRY, whereby this enemy is directed against the armed forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Can we agree, Mr. Theunens, you and I, that the only organs which are supposed to carry out these tasks, are the security organs, and that no other organs can be substituted?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we're talking about the military, yes, it's -- this is the task of the military security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You spoke about the command and control and command functions. Can you explain to us what does the term "command" in professional terms mean?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There may be a translation issue, but are you talking about staff relationship?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me try to put this question slowly for the sake of interpretation. Can you explain to us what the term -- what the term "control" in the technical, professional sense, means?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you talking about relationship that exists between security organs within the JNA, between, for example, security organs of a higher command and a lower command?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Why don't you explain that. Control in the technical, professional sense precisely within the context you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think it's control, but it's probably has to do with the translation, because control in the military means something else. Control means the authority to verify the implementation of -- of assignments, of orders. Control there is a function of command and control. What I understand under the relations between security organs of a higher command and those of a lower command is based on Exhibit 107, paragraphs 18, as well as 57 and 58, where the relationship between, on the one hand, the security administration, so UB, and security organs is explained. And it states that the security administration provides specialised management for security organs. And in addition to that, security organs of a higher command will, in the same manner, provide specialised management to security organs in a lower command. But, as explained in paragraphs 16 and 17 of Exhibit 107, the security organs, or the security organ is directly subordinated to the commanding officer of the command unit, institution or staff of the armed forces in whose strength it is placed in the establishment. And it is also responsible to that officer for its work.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this: When drafting your report, did you come across -- or did you research the book on formations of the guards brigade? Are you aware of such a document? The establishment book of the Guards Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In -- indeed, Your Honours, I'm familiar with this document, and I'm just trying to locate now in which request of which we have requested this from Serbia and Montenegro. In -- on the 16th of June, 2005 we requested from Serbia and Montenegro all documents relating to the organisation and subordination of the Guards Motorised Brigade. We received reply on the 15th of November, 2005 that Serbia and Montenegro was aware they still need to provide an answer to that RFA. There is also the request, 868, from the 17th of June, 2005 where we asked for the SFRY armed forces or JNA rules, regulations or military manuals that were valid in 1991 in relation to the organisation, mission operational concepts for offensive and defensive combat operations, command and control, including responsibility of the commander and other relevant aspects of the Guards Motorised Brigade. We sent in 2005 two reminders. So far we haven't received a reply. And then there is a more recent RFA --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I apologise for interrupting you, but I am not interested at all in learning what you, as the Prosecution, did and how you corresponded with the Council on Cooperation of Serbia and Montenegro. I'm absolutely not interested in that. All I would like to know is whether you saw this document or not. If yes, then say so; if not, once again say so. You know that it exists, but you haven't seen it, right?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: That is correct. Now I'm not one hundred per cent familiar with the specific document you indicate, but I know that for -- like for any other unit in the military, there has to be a regulation that explains how the unit is organised and how it operates. We have requested this document, and we haven't received it. So I haven't seen it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this: Do you know that the motorised guards brigade is quite peculiar in terms of its composition as compared to other brigades that you analysed, infantry, mountain, and all other kinds of brigades that exist. Is it different, and if so, do you know how?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, it is different by its composition. Because -- for example, in the -- the personnel. Only the personnel that matched the highest standards in relation to selection was admitted into the Guards Motorised Brigade. It was also peculiar in its composition because the Guards Motorised Brigade had two military police battalions, including, in the first military police battalion, an anti-terrorist company, which was actually a special military police company, as well as overall the Guards Motorised Brigade was peculiar because of the level of its equipment. And of course, last but not least, it was peculiar because of its subordination. It was subordinated directly to the SSNO, so the federal secretary for people's defence, through the chief of cabinet of the secretariat for people's defence, whereas other motorised battalions -- brigades, most of them were subordinated to corps or to divisions and then to military districts. And this information is included, for example, on page 74, 75 and 76 of the first part of my report, where I base myself on open-source publications from the JNA, namely the Narodna Armija magazine, the article which it can be found in 65 ter 391.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. What about its purpose, the purpose of the motorised guards brigade, did it have some distinctive features too?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. If you allow me, I can read from actually information I found on the internet --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let us please not waste time. The time is very tight, and there are many things I need to ask you. If I ask you to describe its peculiar nature, then please do that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I mean, this comes from the VJ website, because in the absence of documentation from Serbia and Montenegro I looked at the VJ website. And there it says that the Serbian and Montenegrin armed forces guards brigade has in its composition specially selected, trained and equipped units and personal security force to safe-guard the top state and military institutions and personalities. Although it has in its composition combat units of all arms, as well as special units, it is best known for one of its battalions, Honour Guard Battalion. And other information can be found on page 75 in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Will you please tell me, in the command system, what is the position of two military police battalions which are within the motorised guards brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the information I reviewed, these battalions are on equal level as the two motorised battalions that are included in the guards brigade, as well as the armoured battalion and other units, support units, that make up the guards brigade. So they are all subordinated to the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: If there is such a situation where they are directly subordinated to the commander, who then planned and devised the tasks of the military police battalion?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police battalion, like any other battalion in the Guards Motorised Brigade, receives its assignments or its taskings from the commander. The commander, as I have explained in section 6 on planning, has its staff to advise him on how to prepare operations. Now, for the -- for the military police, we know from the security organs regulations that the chief of the security organs is an -- is the advisor to the commander, and in this case the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade, for the use of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, are you familiar with the fact that the staff of the Guards Motorised Brigade included two officers for the military police, two military officers who had the qualifications to deal with the military police forces, and in terms of their competence they were equal to battalion commanders?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question because, I mean, there is an advisor, the security -- chief security organs advises the commanders, i.e., the commander of the guards brigade on how to use the military police. Maybe if you give me names, so it would be easier to refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: We have some interpretation problems. I'll try to rephrase my question. We have some other, perhaps, route to go. What about the brigade staff? Does it not consider a plan for military police activities much the same as when dealing with other battalions within the composition of that brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. It's like any other unit that is included in the -- in the brigade. There will be plans on how to use these units, as well as to regulate other aspects that are related to the activities of these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, would you agree with me that based on these peculiarities of the guards brigade, such as we have just mentioned, resulted in the use of military police in combat operations during the happenings in Vukovar in 1991?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on my review of documents of Operational Group South, it's actually the commander of Operations Group South who determined the use of the military police, including, as you mentioned, the use of the military police in combat operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Is military police otherwise used for combat operations?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would have to look at the manual or the regulation that determined the use of the military police. Now, without looking at the regulations, I can already mention that military police will, for example, be used to assist in traffic control, to escort people, to protect the command post or headquarters, and these kind of tasks can be a component of combat operations. And military -- to continue, military police is explained in part 1 on the pages 84 to 90 of my report, and I mainly refer there to the Exhibit 435.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: What I want to know is: Can military police under what conditions join assault detachments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Based on the orders issued by the commander of OG South, the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what it stands in the regulations concerning the use of the military police?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know -- I'm familiar with these regulations, Your Honour, and it's described in the pages 84 to 90 of the first part of the English version of my report, where the duties of the military police, as well as their subordination and their relation with security organs are explained. There's also an entry for the use of military police in providing security for prisoners of war, in camps for prisoners, as well as their participation in the arrest and escorting of prisoners, also the movements of refugees. And this comes from paragraph 25 of Exhibit 435, the 1985 service regulations of the SFRY military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Now, more about the Guards Motorised Brigade. Do you agree with me when I bear in mind the purpose and the nature of the motorised guards brigade, in terms of their character and their purpose, they were a military police unit, because all its tasks were vintage military police business?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I -- Your Honours, I don't think that's a correct representation of the capabilities of the guards brigade, but because it is correct that the guards brigade had two military police battalions, and it was most known for its duty to protect senior military authorities, but I wish to underline that in addition to the two military police battalions the Guards Motorised Brigade also has two motorised battalions, which are two infantry units with wheeled armoured personnel carriers, as well as an armoured battalion, and that was equipped with M-84 tanks. Military police usually doesn't have tanks to carry out its mission.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Theunens, do you know that from the security organ in the Guards Motorised Brigade there was a military police unit with a special purpose, including 12 officers?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't understand the question, because it says on the transcript: "... from the security organ in the Guards Motorised Brigade there was a military police unit with a special purpose ..." Excuse me, do you mean by this that this military police unit --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
