utterances.text: There, Mr. Theunens. My apologies for overlapping. The poor interpretation is costing a lot of time. I'm trying to speak slowly and to phrase my questions. My question to you was: Are you familiar with the fact that in the Guards Motorised Brigade there was a military police unit used for special purposes made up of 12 officers? If indeed you know about this, say yes. If not, please say no.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you refer to the anti-terrorist unit in --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, no.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, then I'm not familiar with the unit. But I mean from the military point of view, why would you have a unit for special purposes made up of 12 officers?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, Mr. Theunens, Mr. Theunens. Have you had this book, the establishment book of the guards brigade? If you had been given this or if you had otherwise found it, you probably would have understood. I'm not asking this question just because I have nothing better to do. Can you please tell me this, sir: If we have several establishment units within an operations group and each of these has a security organ, what would their mutual relations be? I mean between these security organs belonging to various establishment units, all part of an operations group?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The relations between the security organs belonging to various establishment units, do you mean the relation between the security organs at the level of the command of the operations group on the one hand, and on the other hand, security organs of the subordinate units? Or do you mean the relations between the security organs of the subordinate units? To answer the first question, based on what is written in the regulations that determine the activities of the security organs, there would be a management relationship, what is called special management relation, between the security organs of the command and the security organs of the subordinate units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, specifically: The relations between the security organ of the 80th Motorised Brigade, and the security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer the question specific for the situation in Vukovar, because I don't have documents on that. I can only refer to what I read out earlier in relation to the regulations whereby according to Exhibit 107 there is a special management relationship between the security organs at the higher level, and the security organ at the lower level.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Would you agree with me that the relations between the various security organs within the composition of the establishment units, temporarily part of such an establishment as an operations group, is only in reference to counter-intelligence activity?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed. However, I wish also to draw your attention on the relations that exist between the staffs and the commands of units. In Exhibit 393, which is the 1983 manual for the work of commands and staffs, there is a discussion of the concept of staff relationship whereby, and I will read it out, "Staff relationship" --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, that's a different issue. It's beside the point. I asked you this, I believe we have agreed, under the rules there is no dispute, this is counter-intelligence activity?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. But I wish to add, if you allow, this definition of staff relationships between staffs at a higher level and staffs at a lower level, because it also has an impact on the relationship between security organs of a higher unit and security organs of a lower unit. And if you allow me, I will read out from paragraph 7 from Exhibit 393: "Staff relationships between command organs and staffs at a higher and lower organisational level, are, in fact, functional relationships governed by the principle of obligatory action in accordance with the requests of the staff organ of the superior command for the purpose of implementing the decision made by the superior commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned several times this rule of the security organs in the armed forces of the SFRY. Let me ask you this: Would you agree that a superior officer belonging to a security organ has the power to allow the security organ to only carry out tasks from the purview of the security organ, regardless of the fact whether these tasks are part of any regular activities at the establishment post where he or it happened to be? So tasks from within the purview of a security organ and nothing else. Let me give you a hand. This is Article 48. Or item 48 of the security organ rules.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. If this officer acts as a security organ, and in the -- as part of the framework of his duty of a security organ, he can issue orders or give instructions as has been described by Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who passed this regulation that we're talking about, the security organ rules in the armed forces of the SFRY? The rules of service governing the work of security organs in the armed forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know who passed it, but if we look at -- at the second page of the document, or the first page of the document, it will be explained who signed these rules of service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there is an intervention following consultations with my colleagues. I think on page 90, line 10, 7 to 10, my question number 7 to 10, I asked about the authorised officer, meaning the officer superior to the security organ. The officer superior to the security organ, or to translate, the commander. And I said this was item 48 of the rule. However, I believe the interpretation was poor, so that the answer was in reference to something altogether different.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe the problem could be --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I'm trying to make a much shorter question in a bid to keep it clear and save us from wasting time. The officer superior to the security organ, can this officer to this, his subordinate security organ, give assignments only from the purview of the security organ pursuant to Article 48 of the rules of service of the security organ in the armed forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think it would be helpful if -- if the article of the regulation would be shown, and then we could see it all together. Because this is one -- this is an article I have not included in my report when I discussed the security organs. It's Exhibit 107.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is Exhibit 107. So I would like to -- the B/C/S, page 31. The English, page 19 and 20. I believe 19 is for item 48. For the B/C/S the ERN number is 0090-9832. And the English reference is 0092-0117.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: The English, please. Mr. Theunens, this is page 19. That means 48. Page 19, Article 48, that's where it begins. Can you see that, Mr. Theunens? Do you have that in your screen?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it, yes. Thank you. And it will continue on page 20. But I'm not sure whether this really mentions what you just asked me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Have you got that, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see it, Your Honours, but I'm not sure whether this is --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let's not waste time. In the sense of this legal regulation, Article 48, the rules of service in the armed forces, can you tell me who is the superior officer to the security organ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could we go back to the bottom of page 19, please?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't get the counsel's remark. We're sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I mean, it talks about an authorised officer of a security organ. In my view, it's not the same as the officer who is superior to the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I think this must be a question of poor interpretation. We agree on who is directly superior to the security organ. We agree who has the power to issue assignments to the security organ. My question was just one thing. Can this be the superior officer to the security organ? Can he only issue assignments from the purview of the security organ?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, actually, the Article 16 and 17 in Exhibit 107, so the same regulation, state that: "The security organ is directly subordinate to the commanding officer of the command unit, institution or staff of the armed forces in whose strength it is placed in the establishment and it is responsible to that officer for its work." So --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. I think we -- so that's the superior officer, right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not sure where this superior officer comes from, Mr. Bulatovic. Article 48 in the English version speaks of an authorised officer of a security organ. That indicates, as a matter of language, somebody within the security organ, rather than the commanding officer of the unit who is necessarily outside the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, could we put the B/C/S version on the ELMO, and maybe the translators could read it? It appears that there is a mistake in translation, from what they're doing. From what they're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honours, we can try to do something to clarify this situation regarding the translation. The exhibit number is 107, the B/C/S reference is number 31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will read it out. "In keeping the with duties and obligations under the law and pursuant to regulations based on the law, the authorised officer of the security organ is duty-bound to carry out assignments from the purview of the security organ assigned to him by the relevant officer, regardless of the fact whether these tasks ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think perhaps Mr. Bulatovic, if it helps you, you might give some further thought to Article 48 during the break, which is coming soon, and in the meantime you might like to move on to something else so that you don't lose time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, that is not the problem. The problem is the interpretation, or it seems to be. However, I can press on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think not. Even your interpretation didn't really seem to get you where you wanted to go. So you might have to think about it over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll see about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Can I be clear. Is it your proposition that the commanding officer of a unit, within which there is a security organ, can't give to a security organ any tasks other than those that are within the purview of a security organ?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That, I fear, might be a bit of news to some commanding officers. But nevertheless, it doesn't seem to be borne out by either the English translation or your own translation of Article 48. So if you want to, press on now, but you may find it more useful to go on to something else and think about this over the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll leave this for after the break, but Your Honour, it's just the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I asked you about the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can counsel please speak closer to the microphone or louder. The interpreters are having a lot of trouble hearing him. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This same organ adopted the rules of service governing the work of military police. The question for Mr. Theunens now: Will you agree with me -- Mr. Theunens, will you agree with me that the use of military police outside the prescribed activities in the armed forces can or must be approved by the federal secretary for All People's Defence alone?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't remember seeing such a regulation. But if Mr. Bulatovic can show me the article within the regulations that determine the work of the military police, I would be very willing to look at it. It's possible, but I don't remember seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: I leave that for the break. And then we'll continue after the break. Now let us turn, Mr. Theunens, to a section that has to do with the Zagreb agreement. Do you know at which level the Zagreb agreement was signed -- or, rather, who were the participants in the act of signing the Zagreb agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the people involved in signing the Zagreb agreement for the evacuation of the wounded and the sick of Vukovar Hospital include at least the following people: General Andrija Raseta, who I think was before commander of the 5th Military District or at least a senior military official of the 5th Military District and subsequently was appointed chief negotiator for the JNA. Then there was the Croatian minister of health, Andrija Hebrang. There were also representatives from the ICRC, so the Red Cross. I believe Medecins sans Frontieres and also the Maltezer Kreuz, so NGOs.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can we agree that that was a very high level at which it was signed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Given the importance of that agreement, and also the subject of the agreement, what had to be done in order to prepare the evacuation of the wounded and the sick, as envisaged by the agreement, given the level at which the agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Giving a very general reply to this question, orders should have been issued in order to task those people who were to carry out the evacuation with the assignment of carrying out the evacuation in accordance with what had been agreed in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that since the JNA was involved that there should have been some kind of an order on the evacuation of the wounded and the sick?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours. The only -- actually, I came across two documents that refer to the evacuation of the hospital. The first of all we have Exhibit 415, which is a 1st Military District order, which mentions the task of evacuating the hospital. It is dated the 18th of November. And then there is also an order by OG South, it's 431-9, dated 20th of November, which is Exhibit 419. Now, it is obvious that the 1st Military District, i.e., General Zivota Panic, should have received an order from his superior, that is the Ministry of Defence, the SSNO, in order to implement the agreement that had been signed in Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: When drafting your report and your analysis, did you come across a written order on the evacuation of the wounded and the sick from the Vukovar Hospital pursuant to the agreement which had been signed, which has all the elements prescribed by the agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the two exhibits I just mentioned, 415 and 419, only mention the evacuation of the hospital in as such, so they only say evacuate the hospital. The -- they do not include additional information which would be required to carry out that evacuation in accordance with the agreement signed in Zagreb. Now, for your information, in November 2005 we asked Serbia and Montenegro for all orders by General -- by Colonel Mrksic to ensure the protection and safety of the people who were evacuated from Vukovar Hospital, and the documents we received in January 2006 did not include such an order.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: In your view, given the complexity of evacuation of the wounded and the sick in accordance with the agreement, and bearing in mind the level at which the agreement was signed, what should such an order on evacuation contain?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The order issued by whom? The order issued by the command of the 1st Military District or Operational Group South or the commanding officer who was put in charge of the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you had two documents on evacuation. We also agreed that none of them contained all of the elements prescribed by the agreement of the 18th of November. I'm asking you: An order ordering an evacuation should contain what elements? I'm asking you this as an analyst, given the complexity of the issue.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: An order to -- to carry out an evacuation, i.e., an order to implement the Zagreb agreement would at least include the name of the person who is in charge, i.e., who is in command, the units that would be involved, the mission or task of each of these units, the start of the operation, not only the time, but also the location, the route that would have to be followed by the people -- by the evacuees and the people escorting them, additional coordinating measures in order to ensure that there would be a smooth transition, or at least transport of these people through the zone of operations. It would also have to include the names or the organisation to whom these prisoners should be handed over. There would be an important logistical chapter in order to determine who would provide the vehicles, who would provide food, medical assistance, and so on. There would be a security assessment in order to ascertain the threat of escape of these people who had to be evacuated, as well as an assessment of the risks, possible risks against these prisoners that could be -- that could originate from the local population or any other party that would like to interfere with the evacuation or threaten the physical security of the evacuees. Relating now to the Zagreb agreement, there should be information on the attitude to adopt towards the ICRC and ECMM, if possible the names of the officials of ICRC and ECMM who would be involved in monitoring the evacuation and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me: Prior to the evacuation of the wounded and the sick, given the combat and the armed conflict, was the security organ duty-bound to check the security status at the hospital? You mentioned this in passing just a bit ago.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I would say it would not just be limited to the security status at the hospital itself, but also along the route that would be followed by the evacuees, as well as at the -- the end location of the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that when analysing the documents available to you, among the people at the hospital there were also members of the so-called Croatian army, who had used weapons and had not surrendered like the group of people did on the 18th of November. These people sought shelter in the hospital. We also have information to the effect that they put on white coats trying to disguise themselves as medical staff, that they put on bandages on themselves in order to confuse the perception of their status, and there was this agreement regulating the evacuation of the wounded and the sick from the hospital. These people did this in order to mask the fact that they were members of armed formations who had taken part in combat against the armed forces of the SFRY?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I can only provide an answer to what I understand as being the first part of the question. That is, that indeed according to OG South reports and 1st Military District reports, there were members of the Croatian forces among the people at the hospital. Now, all the other aspects that are mentioned in Mr. Bulatovic's question, I cannot substantiate by documents I came across.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic, is that a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yes. I also need instructions on how much time I have left so that I can go over my questions during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We resume at a quarter to 4.00, and you have 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, let us go back to the matter that wasn't clear, that suffered from poor interpretation and God knows what else. So I'll put the question to you and we'll clarify it. In the Guards Motorised Brigade, who was the immediate superior, or, rather, to whom was Veselin Sljivancanin immediately subordinated?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Major Veselin Sljivancanin was immediately subordinated to the commander of the guards brigade, i.e., Colonel Mile Mrksic in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Does this mean that Mr. Mrksic was the commanding officer with competencies over Veselin Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. But I think "commander" would be a more appropriate translation, but it's maybe a nuance in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's clarify this. Does this mean that Mr. Mrksic, as a superior commanding officer or commander to Mr. Sljivancanin, was entitled to issue certain tasks to his subordinate, Sljivancanin, but only from the domain of security organ's work in accordance with Article 48 that we saw before the break?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to see the Article, because I haven't referred to it in my report, and I -- therefore, I'm -- I was not aware of the limitation in the command authority Mrksic has, as commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade has over the one of his assistant commanders.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: This rule of -- or, rather, Article 48 of the rules of service was admitted into evidence. I see that all of us are giving a different interpretation to it, so let us leave it aside. It will be analysed when the time comes. Now, let me ask you this: There is an evacuation of the wounded and the sick from the Vukovar Hospital, and we have the description of the conditions at the hospital. Evidence was introduced to support that. So under those circumstances, what is the role and participation of the military police in the evacuation of the wounded and the sick? What is the military police supposed to do in that situation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The military police of Operational Group South is supposed to do what the commander of Operations Group South has ordered them to do. And the same applies to military police units of other units that may be involved. It is their commander who will assign a specific task to them, also in relation to the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: The evacuation of the wounded and the sick from the Vukovar Hospital, in accordance with the Zagreb agreement, in terms of its character and the nature of work that was supposed to be done, does it come within the scope of work of the security organs, and is it a task that falls within the scope of work of security organs?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The evacuation of the wounded and sick from the Vukovar Hospital, in accordance with the Zagreb agreement, would be an operation which will require the same kind of planning and preparation as any other military operation. This means that the various staff organs, as well as other departments within the command, and I mean by this, for example, logistics organs and the security organs will assist the commander in preparing orders to implement this evacuation. Now, specifically for the security organs, in addition to what I mentioned before where I spoke about the requirement for the security organs to prepare security assessment which would deal both with the risk of escape or the threat of escape of evacuees or attempts to liberate them, as well as risks to the physical security of the people being evacuated, security organs could also participate in selecting the evacuees, because as you pointed out earlier, they could be civilians, former combatants and other people, and there could be a requirement to make such a selection, and therefore the security organs could assist in this matter too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: Taking people out of the group and frisking them, would that fall under the regular procedure conducted by those escorting detained persons? Are these typical activities, selecting people from a group, frisking them, would that all be part of a regular procedure, conducted by military police when they take a person into custody?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise, I'm not a native English speaker, so the word "frisking" poses some difficulties for me. Maybe there is an easier word.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Searching people.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Visual and physical searching of people.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Yes, indeed. I mean, it should be -- it's part of the order for the evacuation that before evacuating the people they should be searched to prevent, for example, that weapons or other dangerous equipment are taken with the people. Yes. But, again, this is a theoretical which is based on my review of JNA regulations and my own experience or military education. I haven't seen specific orders in relation to how this was carried out during the evacuation of Vukovar Hospital on the 20th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when asked by my learned friend, Mr. Vasic, about the structure of an operations group command, you said that before the command of the guards brigade took over the command of the OG South, Colonel Pavkovic and Colonel Terzic came, that they were sent to the command. I'd like to know whether I noted this down correctly and, if so, would you please explain in what capacity these two senior officers came. They held the rank of colonel. They were sent from the office of the Federal Secretariat for All People's Defence, and they were sent to the operations group.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, what I mentioned to Mr. Vasic, and what is also included in my report on page 65 in the English version, the second part, I made reference to Exhibit 404, which talks about the assignment of Colonel Nebojsa Pavkovic -- a temporary assignment, and Colonel Zlatoje Terzic to the Guards Motorised Brigade. So not to OG South from the [indiscernible], but to the Guards Motorised Brigade, and this order dates from the 29th of September, 1991. My understanding is that these two officers were sent to carry out liaison tasks which is not an unusual occurrence in such a situation, based on my experience. Now, maybe we should look at Exhibit 404 to know the -- to see the exact phrasing of Colonel Vuk Obradovic's order to temporarily reassign Pavkovic and Terzic to the command of the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, when writing your report, did you take into account -- rather, were documents made available to you, documents of the ECMM monitors who followed the evacuation of the wounded and the sick, who monitored it. I didn't find such reference in your report, so I'd like to know this from you.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did take these reports into my account -- into account, excuse me, to prepare this report. But I thought it was -- as an analyst, I thought it was more useful to confine myself to the reporting of Operational Group South and the 1st Military District on how they implemented the evacuation, not only the evacuation of the hospital, but also other evacuation operations that were taking place during that time period in Vukovar. And I confined myself because it were actually 1st Military District and OG South who carried out the operation who should actually be best placed to know how the evacuations went.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Did you find in those reports that Nebojsa Pavkovic played a certain role in the evacuation of the wounded and the sick and the implementation of the Zagreb agreement?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that he played a role based on video imagery I have seen, including the famous Borsinger video, but I haven't used that for my report. Otherwise, I would not be able to answer the -- otherwise, I would not be able to answer the question, unless you would show me these documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Theunens, I didn't ask you about video footage. I asked you about the reports of the EC monitors. Did you have them in your hands when drafting your report or not?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I mentioned earlier that I did take these reports into account. I read them. I also understood, but I'm not clear which specific report it was, but that in one of the reports there was a confusion or a mixing up of names between Pavkovic and Sljivancanin. But again, if you wish me to comment on ECMM reports, I think it would be useful for all of us if you would show that report to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we put Exhibit 316 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have it, Mr. Theunens?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indeed, Your Honours, I have it in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Can you see what is written under the heading "Subject." Negotiations of the evacuation of wounded people from the Vukovar Hospital; correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Would you like to look at the names of participants,, the last four persons on -- are on behalf of the JNA. I will read out the names and you can follow. I'm not going to mention the monitors of the EC. It says here: Participants, Colonel Pavkovic, JNA commander for the Operations Group South, Vukovar; Colonel Loncar, liaison officer of the JNA within the 1st Military District; Colonel Memisevic, liaison officer of the JNA within the 1st Military District; and Major Zaric -- it says here Saric but it should be Zaric, liaison officer of the JNA within the 1st Military District. Correct?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, you have read out the information as it is mentioned in the document, but the definition of Colonel Pavkovic as JNA commander, Operations Group South is in contradiction with the Operations Group South documents we have for the time period. So there must be a misunderstanding somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Theunens, all I'm doing is reading what this gentleman, Mr. Cunningham, a member of the ECMM, wrote. I don't want to waste any more time on this. Now, let's turn to page 2 of this report, I'd like to read paragraph d to you, second page of this report. It says here in paragraph d: "Paragraph 5 of the fax signed by Croats and the JNA evoked much discussion. Colonel Pavkovic stated that prisoners of war would not be allowed to depart as the POWs are under the JNA control. If he did, Serb irregulars/local citizens would attack the convoy." And (3): "At some future time the POWs would be exchanged for the JNA POWs." Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honours. Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we pull up Exhibit 333?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, if you allow me, I would still like to finish my reply, actually, in relation to the questions on Pavkovic. Colonel Pavkovic is obviously sent as the negotiator for Operational Group South, i.e., he has been mandated, authorised by the commander of OG South or somebody who is superior to the commander of OG South, and the views Pavkovic expressed cannot be his personal views but they are the views as they have been defined by the JNA, and also reflected in the instructions the commander of OG South must have given to Pavkovic before he started to negotiate with ECMM.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Exhibit 333. See here, please look at item 1 of this report. I will read this out, and you can follow to make sure I'm reading correctly. You have the English version. It says there: "On arrival at the headquarters Colonel Pavkovic, in Negoslavci, we discussed once again contentious issues that we had discussed on the previous day. Colonel Pavkovic remained firm that not all the wounded would be evacuated. As a result of an order of General Raseta, Croatian paramilitaries who were wounded would remain as POWs." Have I read this out correctly?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: A bit earlier when I asked you about the Zagreb agreement you mentioned Mr. Raseta. You said who he was and what he was. Let me ask you this: Mr. Mrksic, as the commander of the Operations Group South, was he able to issue an order to General Raseta?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It all depends of the situation they're in. I mean, it would be unusual that a colonel issues an order to a general, but it can be that there is, for example -- I mean, I'm giving a theoretical scenario now, that a general is visiting an -- the headquarters of the colonel, and the colonel is in charge of the operation, and then the colonel could issue an order to the general to -- to leave the area, for example. I mean, it's not a good example. But if they're not the same chain of command -- if they are in the same chain of command, excuse me, then a colonel cannot issue an order to a general. But I'm not really sure what you're asking in this context.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing more than I asked. If we know that Mr. Raseta is the commander of the 5th District, can the commander of OG South issue an order to him. But that's all right, we've discussed that already. Something else in relation to this report. We have seen reports produced by ECMM containing information highly relevant to the evacuation of the sick and wounded. Did you believe them to be entirely irrelevant to your report, since there is not a single word in your report about these ECMM reports?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, it's not a question of relevant or irrelevant, but having access to what I would call the primary sources, i.e., the documents prepared by the people that were directly involved in carrying out the evacuation. And I mean by this the 1st Military District and Operational Group South. I didn't really see a need to include reports that were actually drafted by people who were only observers to the whole process but not directly involved in its execution. Because I'm pretty sure that if I had included only the ECMM documents, or also the ECMM documents, you would have said, well, why do you include the ECMM documents if you have already the JNA documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: These are relevant documents, Mr. Pringle [sic]. There are at least the quality level of some articles from a newspaper called Greater Serbia, which you found fit to mention in your analysis. Let me ask you something else.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is it a question or is it a comment? Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: My apologies, my apologies. I have overstepped the mark. I would like to ask you something else. Speaking of the interview, you mentioned in your report an interview with Zivota Panic, in which you say that Zivota Panic, in this interview, said that Veselin Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. But it's not me who says that. It's actually according to the transcript at least of the interview, and it's also available on videotape, it is Zivota Panic who makes that statement. And it's on the page 92 in my report, and in the document it should be on the page 04 -- 0460-7856 in the English transcript of the interview that Zivota Panic provided to the BBC series "Death of Yugoslavia." And if you allow me, the reason why I include this interview, because we didn't obtain any documents on whether -- the role of Sljivancanin in the evacuation, but I'm familiar with the statement Veselin Sljivancanin gave to the Belgrade military prosecutor in 1998 in which he mentioned that he was in charge of the evacuation of Vukovar Hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have to object to this part of the expert's answer. Because he can't use a statement that was given to the OTP that we don't have here and about which we still haven't resolved the question of how that statement would be used. The fact is Veselin Sljivancanin has not appeared in any role here except as an accused, but these comments in this sort of preparation clearly point to something else, and we would move that this part of the witness's answer not be taken into account. The page is 0460-7856 and if that could please be read out, and this is a relevant passage, just to see if the interpretation here in this report is accurate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you referring to an interview with the BBC, or to what is said to be evidence or a statement given to the Belgrade military prosecutor?

utterances.speaker: MS. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is a --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an interview with Zivota Panic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel switch the microphone on or start speaking into the microphone. The interpreters can hear nothing at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, there were two microphones on at the same time. Apparently in his interview for the "Death of Yugoslavia," the BBC series, Zivota Panic stated that Major Veselin Sljivancanin had been in charge of the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital. It is the Defence team's position that Zivota Panic made no such reference to the evacuation in that interview. Can the relevant portion therefore please be read out to see what lies at heart of the matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. DOKMANOVIC
utterances.text: "But we did not bomb the hospital, and the moment our troops entered that compound Sljivancanin was in charge of that operation. But after that, International Red Cross interfered and you know what happened later. A part of the wounded was tran -- pull out by then. Some were transported to our hospitals."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's your contention, is it, Mr. Bulatovic, that that interview does not support the proposition that your client was in charge of the evacuation operation?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, I can't accept that my client was in charge of the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital. Secondly, I submit that there is no reference to an evacuation here in this transcript. Not the way we have seen it here. Now -- or in Mr. Theunens's report, for that matter. I'll try to wrap this up quickly now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That concern will be considered in due course, Mr. Bulatovic. Now, you are already overrun by five minutes, so your wrap-up will need to be immediate.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question. I have plenty left, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: You quote a piece from some newspaper or other, Daily Telegraph, Branislav Vakic, a Chetnik Vojvoda. He said that Veselin Sljivancanin gave them weapons and that they worked with him and so on and so forth. Did you have the original piece? Did you ever see the original piece published in the Telegraph newspaper? And did you consider Mr. Vakic's diary or log-book when you included this in your report?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the article is indeed -- or extracts of the article are included in my report. Why, because I considered them useful in the context of this report. Now, Vakic gives a long overview not only of his involvement in Vukovar, but also in other areas, and I was able to corroborate large sections of the interview Vakic provided with other military documents I had come across in other cases. And I'm aware of the time constraints but, for example, Vakic talks about his involvement in the Skelani area in Bosnia-Herzegovina, or in eastern Bosnia-Herzegovina, in early 1993 and --

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, all I asked was whether he had the original piece in his possession, the one that he invokes, and why do we not have it, the one from the Telegraph newspaper. We have transcripts of conversations that cannot be attributed to anyone in particular, or timed at any particular time.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This interview is 65 ter number 628, and it's my understanding that it's -- I'm sorry, it's not -- it's -- I apologise, it's a correction. The interview is 65 ter number 612, and we only have the English version here at the ICTY. But I'm very willing to look at the B/C/S version and to see whether there are any discrepancies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, ideally I would have lots of questions left. However, clearly you are in charge of this courtroom, which means this concludes my cross-examination. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Bulatovic. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll move fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness please be shown Exhibit 107 -- I'm sorry, Exhibit 107, Article 48. I'm going to read in part from a copy of that. "An authorised officer of a security organ -- of a security organ is obliged to carry out tasks within the competence of the security organ that a competent officer assigns to him, regardless of whether or not these tasks are covered by the work that is regularly conducted in their establishment position." Is there anything in that quotation that would prevent a commander of an operational group from ordering or assigning the head of a security organ to command a military operation?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours. Based on -- on this article, there is not. Because I would refer then actually to what we saw earlier about delegation, that a commander can appoint or can delegate some of his powers to any officer he deems competent to carry out these powers, and security officers are also part of the -- or this also applies to security officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if a commander of a operational group wanted to place a -- the command -- the chief of a security organ in charge of an evacuation operation, is that possible?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, and by this appointment the chief of the security organ would become a commanding officer, i.e., an officer in command of that evacuation operation, as any other officer who would have been put in such a position, by the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Let's move on to a couple other issues. You were shown a few minutes ago Exhibit 316, and it mentioned that the POWs are under the control of the JNA and it also indicated that Serb irregulars/local citizens would attack the convoy if these POWs are removed or placed on the convoy. Now, you previously discussed planning and the duty to predict and forecasting yesterday. If the person in charge of an evacuation or the commanding officer receives notice that some of the people to be evacuated are in danger of Serb irregulars or the local citizens, what is his or her duty?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, his duty would be to prevent, in this case, the Serb irregulars from endangering the evacuees. So in the preparation of the operation he would make sure that he makes forces available and includes taskings for these forces to be ready to counter any threat that is posed to the physical security of the evacuees.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And how much police units do the Guards Motorised Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean -- I think you mean military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Military police units.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Guards Motorised Brigade had two military police battalions, and in -- I think it was in October the Guards Motorised Brigade received a company with an additional 100 men of military police. It is mentioned in the report, but maybe because of time constraints I will not be able to identify the correct page within reasonable limits.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's sufficient, as long as you've indicated it's mentioned in the report, sir. Now, let's just move on to another issue. There was some discussion of Vukovar being taken on or about the 18th, or on the 18th. And there was an issue of whether or not there was still a need for assault detachments. When Vukovar was taken on the 18th, did that mean that all resistance had ended in the area?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honours, it didn't mean that. And this is, for example, obvious from orders issued by the 1st -- by the commander of the 1st Military District on and after the 18th of November, where in one of these orders he -- Panic mentions that the war is not over. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So there was no need to immediately remove the assault detachments or resubordinate the assault detachments?

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I mean, from a purely theoretical point of view, maintaining the assault detachments as well as the assault groups, made it easier to maintain command and control over all the forces that were included in the operational group. And we have discussed already earlier the orders of -- the particular order from the 18th of November of Zivota Panic, Exhibit 415, where he warns for the risk of revenge and retribution by elements of the local Serb Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, there was some discussion, or I think three or four times you mentioned during the testimony that the TOs in Vukovar were not the TOs envisioned in the rules. And you mentioned that in relation to their numbers and their content. What do you mean by that? You never explained that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first section of my report, Your Honours, I discussed Territorial Defence in -- I mean, the first part of the report in the sections [sic] 5, for example, page 92 and following pages, where also the structure is defined, as well as the types of TO units. Now, what we see in Vukovar, and I will limit myself to Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora, which are discussed from page 79 onwards, second part, English version. We see from various documentation both from OG South and the most obvious example is the resubordination order from the 21st in the morning, where an order for the resubordination of Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora is sent to, among others, the commander of the Seseljevci. I've also included, indeed as pointed out by Mr. Bulatovic,, references to the newspaper of the Serbian Radical Party, Velika Srbija, whereby -- in which the links between Leva Supoderica and the Serbian Radical Party are highlighted, where -- calling Leva Supoderica a -- I quote, "Chetnik detachment." So this all shows that actually these Leva Supoderica and Petrova Gora detachments could only be considered TO by their name but not by their nature, nor by their structure, nor by is even more important, their motivation to participate in the operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the final area, you indicated that a operational group commander would not usually tell an assault detachment commander how to organise its companies. Does this mean that an assault detachment commander would have some independence in the establishment of his companies, the numbers, the units involved? Can you please explain that.

utterances.speaker: REYNAUD THEUNENS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Within the military each unit commander is responsible for the use of his unit towards his superior who has issued an assignment to him for the use of that unit. So if the assault -- if the operational group commander issues an order for a particular task to the assault detachment commander, based on the documents I reviewed, it will be the assault detachment commander who will determine how he will use his own forces, i.e., his companies in this case, or his assault groups on how to implement the tasking he has received from the operational group commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Weiner. We have concluded the evidence of this witness. May we thank you, Mr. Theunens, for the assistance you've given, and for your report. And we now adjourn to resume tomorrow at 9.30. The witness tomorrow, if we could catch up the theme of last week, ought to be a witness that can be completed in less than a full day. And if that is achieved, there will be more time for the evidence of the remaining expert witness, who could commence evidence tomorrow afternoon. So it's in the hands of -- Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sorry to notify you, but apparently there is a bit of a problem. General Pringle has to fly back tonight to Great Britain, but will return tomorrow evening. He will not be available tomorrow afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's paid to that plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The best-laid plans of mice and men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, all right. Two days, we can see how tight two days is, and we will just have to be very disciplined in time. If there are any other procedural matters that need to be dealt with, they can be raised tomorrow afternoon when we finish the evidence of the one witness. We will adjourn now until 9.30 tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 21st day of June, 2006, at 9.30 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.33 p.m.,
